I have two Obsidian vaults with a lot of notes. I asked Claude, “Look thru my Obsidian vaults and find examples where I contradict myself”.
First Vault
I’ll help you explore your Obsidian vault to identify contradictions in your thinking. Let me start by getting an overview of your vault structure and then examine the content systematically.Based on my exploration of your Obsidian vault, I’ve identified several fascinating tensions in your thinking that reveal the complexity of your intellectual development. Rather than simple contradictions, these seem more like unresolved philosophical tensions you’re working through:
The Power Paradox
In “Power and Personal Influence,” you write that power and influence “can corrupt the soul” but also argue that “a desire to have some power and influence is not a fundamentally bad thing.” Yet in your Vipassana reflections, you champion equanimity and non-attachment. Meanwhile, in “Digital Disobedience,” you advocate for actively “seizing” digital real estate and creating lasting personal legacy.
This suggests you’re wrestling with a fundamental question: Can one seek influence and create legacy while maintaining spiritual detachment? You seem to want power for creative/generative purposes while being wary of its corrupting effects.
The Digital Engagement Dilemma
You simultaneously advocate for thoughtful digital participation (creating “digital footprints” as a form of conscious legacy-building) while criticizing how we’ve become “conditioned to react with likes, dislikes, and millions of emojis.” You want to use digital tools for meaningful intellectual work while rejecting the reactive culture they create.
This reflects a deeper tension: How do you engage meaningfully with systems whose fundamental nature you find problematic?
The Action vs. Acceptance Tension
Your Vipassana writings emphasize accepting limitations, observing without reacting, and finding equanimity. But your other writings show active engagement - you initiate calls with parents when “patience runs out,” advocate for “digital disobedience,” and clearly believe in taking action to create change.
You seem to be trying to integrate Eastern philosophy’s emphasis on acceptance with Western ideals of active engagement and personal agency.
The Knowledge Paradox
In “The Right Age,” you question the value of consuming content (movies, books) without retention or emotional attachment. Yet throughout your vault, you advocate for extensive intellectual output and public participation. You’re critical of passive consumption while championing active creation.
The Individual vs. Collective Focus
Your happiness essay suggests finding fulfillment through contributing to others, while your legacy writings are intensely self-focused. This seems to reflect an ongoing negotiation between altruistic and self-actualizing approaches to meaning.
These aren’t necessarily flaws - they might represent the natural evolution of someone thinking seriously about complex philosophical questions. The tensions suggest you’re working through fundamental questions about how to live meaningfully in the modern world while maintaining spiritual and intellectual integrity.
What strikes me is that rather than settling into dogmatic positions, you seem to be genuinely grappling with the inherent contradictions of conscious living. The question might not be resolving these tensions but learning to hold them creatively.

You write extensively about “metascience entrepreneurship” and changing scientific institutions, but you’re also actively participating in and seeking funding from those same institutions. This suggests a tension between wanting to reform systems from within while maintaining autonomy.

data.title: My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now (GLM-4.5 Air)
data.author: simonw
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在2.5年前的笔记本电脑上使用GLM-4.5 Air模型和MLX库成功运行了一个可以编写JavaScript版《太空入侵者》游戏的实验。GLM-4.5模型由中国Z.ai公司发布，具备较高的编码能力。作者通过Ivan Fioravanti优化的44GB版本，在64GB内存的MacBook Pro M2上运行该模型，生成了完整的HTML和JavaScript游戏代码，且无需额外编辑即可运行。尽管模型运行时占用了约48GB内存，但其表现非常出色。作者还对比了两年前LLaMA模型的表现，感叹2025年本地运行的高质量编码模型已取得显著进步。
data.comments_summary:

44723316.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
My 2.5 year old laptop can write Space Invaders in JavaScript now, using GLM-4.5 Air and MLX
29th July 2025
I wrote about the new
GLM-4.5
model family yesterday—new open weight (MIT licensed) models from
Z.ai
in China which their benchmarks claim score highly in coding even against models such as Claude Sonnet 4.
The models are pretty big—the smaller GLM-4.5 Air model is still 106 billion total parameters, which
is 205.78GB
on Hugging Face.
Ivan Fioravanti
built
this
44GB 3bit quantized version for MLX
, specifically sized so people with 64GB machines could have a chance of running it. I tried it out... and it works
extremely well
.
I fed it the following prompt:
Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders
And it churned away for a while and produced
the following
:
Clearly this isn’t a particularly novel example, but I still think it’s noteworthy that a model running on my 2.5 year old laptop (a 64GB MacBook Pro M2) is able to produce code like this—especially code that worked first time with no further edits needed.
How I ran the model
I had to run it using the current
main
branch of the
mlx-lm
library (to ensure I had
this commit
adding
glm4_moe
support). I ran that using
uv
like this:
uv run \
--with
'
https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/archive/489e63376b963ac02b3b7223f778dbecc164716b.zip
'
\
python
Then in that Python interpreter I used the standard recipe for running MLX models:
from
mlx_lm
import
load
,
generate
model
,
tokenizer
=
load
(
"mlx-community/GLM-4.5-Air-3bit"
)
That downloaded 44GB of model weights to my
~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--mlx-community--GLM-4.5-Air-3bit
folder.
Then:
prompt
=
"Write an HTML and JavaScript page implementing space invaders"
messages
=
[{
"role"
:
"user"
,
"content"
:
prompt
}]
prompt
=
tokenizer
.
apply_chat_template
(
messages
,
add_generation_prompt
=
True
)
response
=
generate
(
model
,
tokenizer
,
prompt
=
prompt
,
verbose
=
True
,
max_tokens
=
8192
)
The response started like this:
<think>
The user wants me to create a Space Invaders game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. I need to create a complete, functional game with the following features:
Player spaceship that can move left/right and shoot
Enemy invaders that move in formation and shoot back
Score tracking
Lives/health system
Game over conditions [...]
Followed by the HTML and this debugging output:
Prompt: 14 tokens, 14.095 tokens-per-sec
Generation: 4193 tokens, 25.564 tokens-per-sec
Peak memory: 47.687 GB
You can see
the full transcript here
, or view
the source on GitHub
, or
try it out in your browser
.
A pelican for good measure
I ran
my pelican benchmark
against the full sized models
yesterday
, but I couldn’t resist trying it against this smaller 3bit model. Here’s what I got for
"Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle"
:
Here’s the
transcript for that
.
In both cases the model used around 48GB of RAM at peak, leaving me with just 16GB for everything else—I had to quit quite a few apps in order to get the model to run but the speed was pretty good once it got going.
Local coding models are really good now
It’s interesting how almost every model released in 2025 has specifically targeting coding. That focus has clearly been paying off: these coding models are getting
really good
now.
Two years ago when I
first tried LLaMA
I never
dreamed
that the same laptop I was using then would one day be able to run models with capabilities as strong as what I’m seeing from GLM 4.5 Air—and Mistral 3.2 Small, and Gemma 3, and Qwen 3, and a host of other high quality models that have emerged over the past six months.

• joelthelion：询问除Mac之外，是否有其他设备能以合理性能运行LLM推理。
• __mharrison__：计划更换笔记本电脑以适应本地LLM运行需求，当前的16GB内存不足。
• joshstrange：计划升级SSD以存储更多模型和数据，对本地运行大模型有实际需求。
• pamelafox：现有的16GB RAM的Mac无法满足运行大模型的需求，只能使用较小参数的模型（如llama3.1:8b）。
• efitz：误解文章主题，以为是关于教小孩编程的文章，未深入讨论技术。
• bradly：对文章提供的聊天记录和源代码表示赞赏，并建议后续添加功能（如高分榜）。同时提到Space Invaders的知识产权问题，提醒法律风险。
• neutronicus：询问如果理解正确，作者是否是在64GB RAM的笔记本上运行模型，并推测64GB+ RAM的家用工作站也能达到类似效果。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及本地运行LLM的硬件需求（如RAM和SSD）以及不同设备的适用性（如Mac与其他设备）。
• 涉及知识产权问题，尤其是经典游戏Space Invaders的合法性讨论。
• 对本地运行模型的基准测试工具和排行榜存在需求，希望有更系统化的测试方法。
• 对商业模式的未来影响（如本地运行高质量模型对收费服务商的挑战）也有讨论。

data.title: Project Zero – Policy and Disclosure: 2025 Edition
data.author: esnard
data.article_summary: Google Project Zero 更新了其漏洞披露政策，引入"报告透明度试验"以解决"上游补丁差距"问题。该差距指上游厂商已修复漏洞，但下游依赖方尚未将其整合至最终产品，导致补丁到达用户设备的时间延迟。新政策要求在向厂商报告漏洞后一周内公开披露漏洞信息，包括受影响的产品和披露截止日期，但不包含技术细节。此举旨在通过提高透明度，促进上下游之间的沟通，加快补丁开发和采用速度。试验保持原有的90+30天披露期限，预期能缩短漏洞修复周期，同时避免为攻击者提供便利。谷歌将密切监控试验效果，以实现更安全的生态系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google政策变化及其在漏洞披露和修复过程中的影响

不同观点：
• woodruffw: 支持政策变化，理解P0团队在让供应商认真对待补丁方面的困难。不过担心公开披露漏洞信息可能为攻击者提供有价值的信息，特别是在开源项目中，完全保密漏洞是非常困难的。
• tptacek: 赞赏此举，认为这是对经典漏洞研究者“透明报告”过程的重新表述。通过发布确认漏洞的报告 artifact，能增加透明度。
• jms703: 认为这是一个好的举措，希望软件的缓慢使用者能够提前预见即将发布的版本并制定补救计划，而不是在发布后才进行处理。

• runningmike: 认为过度关注开源软件安全而忽视闭源硬件、固件和软件的安全问题。过多的指责和压力无助于解决复杂问题，质疑Google是否在慢慢“杀死”开源软件。
• bgwalter: 认为提醒下游的目标有点奇怪，建议Project Zero可以通过建立信任的下游邮件列表来发布新发现的公告。认为真正的目标是增加对上游的压力。
• riedel: 关注Google内部产品（如Google Bigwave）的披露问题。
• amiga386: 提到Google可能借鉴了rachelbythebay的模糊发布做法，担心这种做法会导致无根据的猜测和恐慌，不希望Google的实验出现类似问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于公开披露漏洞信息的价值与风险之间的平衡。一些评论担心这种做法会为攻击者提供便利，而另一些评论则认为增加透明度是必要的。
• 另一个讨论点是此政策是否适用于Google自己的产品，以及如何衡量此政策变化的成功与否。
• 还有对开源软件与闭源软件安全关注度的不同看法，反映了对整体安全策略的更广泛关注。

44724287.article_content:
Posted by Tim Willis, Google Project Zero
In 2021, we updated our vulnerability disclosure policy to the current "90+30" model. Our goals were to drive faster yet thorough patch development, and improve patch adoption. While we’ve seen progress, a significant challenge remains: the time it takes for a fix to actually reach an end-user's device.
This delay, often called the "patch gap," is a complex problem. Many consider the patch gap to be the time between a fix being released for a security vulnerability and the user installing the relevant update.
However, our work has highlighted a critical, earlier delay: the
"upstream patch gap"
.
This is the period where an upstream vendor has a fix available, but downstream dependents, who are ultimately responsible for shipping fixes to users, haven’t yet integrated it into their end product.
As Project Zero's recent work has focused on foundational, upstream technologies like chipsets and their drivers, we've observed that this upstream gap significantly extends the vulnerability lifecycle.
For the end user, a vulnerability isn't fixed when a patch is released from Vendor A to Vendor B; it's only fixed when they download the update and install it on their device. To shorten that entire chain, we need to address the upstream delay.
To address this, we're announcing a new trial policy:
Reporting Transparency
.
The Trial: Reporting Transparency
Our core
90-day disclosure deadline
will remain in effect. However, we're adding a new step at the beginning of the process.
Beginning today,
within one week of reporting a vulnerability to a vendor,
we will
publicly share
that a vulnerability was discovered. We will share:
The vendor or open-source project that received the report.
The affected product.
The date the report was filed, and when the 90-day disclosure deadline expires.
This trial maintains our existing 90+30 policy, meaning vendors still have 90 days to fix a bug before it is disclosed, with a 30-day period for patch adoption if the bug is fixed before the deadline.
Google Big Sleep, a collaboration between Google DeepMind and Google Project Zero, will also be trialling this policy for their vulnerability reports. The issue tracker for Google Big Sleep is at
goo.gle/bigsleep
Why the Change? Increased Transparency to Close the Gap
The primary goal of this trial is to shrink the upstream patch gap by increasing transparency. By providing an early signal that a vulnerability has been reported upstream, we can better inform downstream dependents. For our small set of issues, they will have an additional source of information to monitor for issues that may affect their users.
We hope that this trial will encourage the creation of stronger communication channels between upstream vendors and downstream dependents relating to security, leading to faster patches and improved patch adoption for end users.
This data will make it easier for researchers and the public to track how long it takes for a fix to travel from the initial report, all the way to a user's device (which is especially important if the fix never arrives!)
Will this help attackers?
No
— w
e anticipate that in the initial phase of this trial, there may be increased public attention on unfixed bugs. We want to be clear:
no technical details, proof-of-concept code, or information that we believe would materially assist discovery will be released
until the deadline. Reporting Transparency is an alert, not a blueprint for attackers.
We understand that for some vendors without a downstream ecosystem, this policy may create unwelcome noise and attention for vulnerabilities that only they can address. However, these vendors now represent the minority of vulnerabilities reported by Project Zero. We believe the benefits of a fair, simple, consistent and transparent policy outweigh the risk of inconvenience to a small number of vendors.
That said, in 2025, we hope that the industry consensus is that the mere existence of vulnerabilities in software is neither surprising nor alarming. End users are more aware of the importance of security updates than ever before. It's widely accepted as fact that any system of moderate complexity will have vulnerabilities, and systems that were considered impenetrable in the past have been shown to be vulnerable in retrospect.
This is a trial, and we will be closely monitoring its effects. We hope it achieves our ultimate goal: a safer ecosystem where vulnerabilities are remediated not just in an upstream code repository, but
on the devices
, systems and services that people use every day. We look forward to sharing our findings and continuing to evolve our policies to meet the challenges of the ever-changing security landscape.

data.title: Show HN: ELF Injector
data.author: dillstead
data.article_summary:
ELF Injector 是一个工具，能够在 32-bit ARM 处理器上向 ELF 可执行文件注入可重定位代码片段，并在原程序入口点之前执行。该工具通过命令行使用，格式为 `elf_injector <exec> <chunk> <entry offset>`，其中 `exec` 是目标可执行文件，`chunk` 是要注入的二进制代码，`entry offset` 是代码执行的起始偏移。

该工具提供了三个示例代码片段：
1. `greeting`：输出 "Hello World"。
2. `startup_dump`：输出命令行参数、环境变量、辅助向量和注入信息。
3. `copy_chunk`：随机选择一个可执行文件进行自我注入并输出文件名。

`inject_info` 结构用于传递注入信息，包含片段位置、长度和执行起始偏移等数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ELF文件代码注入的技术与挑战

不同观点：
• [nekitamo] 分享了自己十年前为Android .so库编写二进制打包器的经验。他通过移动Pheaders来为Elf32_Phdr表腾出空间，并在文件末尾注入新的代码段，但这种方法会因为填充字节增加文件大小。他还提到通过在动态段（DT_INIT）中指定新代码执行顺序，避免修改入口点指针。他赞赏了另一种使用thunk的解决方案，认为它更简洁高效。此外，他提到可以完全移除ELF文件的段表头，因为操作系统只需要段头即可执行文件。

• [Retr0id] 提出ELF注入/感染的一个挑战是可能会打破原ELF文件的布局假设，特别是在处理动态ELF时（例如那些在运行时解析.dynamic段的文件）。他还询问了该方法在不同目标ELF文件上的适用性及是否存在不兼容的情况。

• [viccis] 关注该技术在安全软件（如VirusTotal）上的表现，担心这种打包或混淆技术会被恶意软件利用，从而遭到安全软件的激进标记和拦截。

• [etune] 提到了一种基于ATOM技术的代码注入方法，可以在程序的任何基本块之前或之后注入代码。这种技术通过替换基本块的第一条指令为跳转指令来实现，跳转到包含新代码的区域，执行后再跳回原指令。

• [matheusmoreira] 讨论了一种无需文件I/O的代码注入方法，利用了/proc/self/exe来定位可执行文件，并通过ELF段和auxvec让内核将数据映射到内存中。他还提到自己创建了一个ELF嵌入工具，可以嵌入任意数据，并建议通过自检ELF头的方式找到合适的段，进而加载数据和代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是不同ELF文件注入代码的兼容性问题，[Retr0id]对此提出了疑问。
• [nekitamo] 和 [matheusmoreira] 都提到了利用ELF段来实现代码注入，但方法不同，前者侧重于移动段表头，后者则利用内核映射功能。
• 安全性和反病毒软件的检测是另一个值得注意的讨论点，[viccis] 提到了该技术在反病毒环境下的潜在问题。
• 技术实现的复杂性和优化也是讨论的一个重点，[nekitamo] 和 [etune] 都提到了不同方法的复杂度和效率问题。

ELF Injector
Injects a relocatable code chunk of arbitrary size into an
ELF
executable that will run before the original entry point of the executable.
Building
NOTE
: The code can only build and run on a
32-bit ARM
processor as it contains a mix of C and assembly.
Build
elf_injector
:
~/elf_injector $ make all
gcc -Werror -std=gnu99 -fno-builtin -Wall -Wextra -O2 -c src/elf_injector.c -o elf_injector.o
gcc -nostdlib elf_injector.o -o elf_injector
gcc -Werror -std=gnu99 -fno-builtin -Wall -Wextra  -O2 -c src/test.c -o test.o
gcc test.o -o test
~/elf_injector $
Build the relocatable code
chunks
:
~/elf_injector $ cd chunks
~/elf_injector $ make all
cc -Werror -std=gnu99 -fno-builtin -Wall -Wextra -nostdlib -mgeneral-regs-only -fpie -O2 -o greeting_strip greeting_strip.c
objdump -d -S greeting_strip > greeting_strip.asm
objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text greeting_strip greeting_strip.bin
cc -Werror -std=gnu99 -fno-builtin -Wall -Wextra -nostdlib -mgeneral-regs-only -fpie -O2 -o startup_dump_strip startup_dump_strip.c
objdump -d -S startup_dump_strip > startup_dump_strip.asm
objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text startup_dump_strip startup_dump_strip.bin
cc -Werror -std=gnu99 -fno-builtin -Wall -Wextra -nostdlib -mgeneral-regs-only -fpie -O2 -o copy_chunk_strip copy_chunk_strip.c
objdump -d -S copy_chunk_strip > copy_chunk_strip.asm
objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text copy_chunk_strip copy_chunk_strip.bin
~/elf_injector $
Running
The
elf_injector
command line utility inserts a code
chunk
into  an ELF executable and has a simple command line interface:
~/elf_injector $ ./elf_injector
usage: elf_injector <exec> <chunk> <entry offset>
exec
is the executable to inject the
chunk
into.  It must be an executable, not a shared library.
chunk
is a binary file containing the code to inject, and
entry_offset
is the offset in bytes from the beginning of the
chunk
from which to start execution.  The resulting output file is the same name as
exec
albeit with a
.injected
extension.
The chunks directory contains three sample
chunks
that can be injected into executables:
greeting
,
startup_dump
, and
copy_chunk
The entry offsets are
0
,
112
,
1640
respectively.
greeting
greeting
outputs
"Hello World\n"
to
stdout
:
~/elf_injector $ ./test
Testing 123...
~/elf_injector $ ./elf_injector test chunks/greeting_strip.bin 0
inserted 280 byte thunk at pos 1484, start 0x678
inserted 120 byte chunk at pos 1764, start 0x6e4
~/elf_injector $ ./test.injected
Hello World
Testing 123...
~/elf_injector $
startup_dump
startup_dump
outputs the command line arguments, environment,
auxiliary vector
, and
inject_info
to
stdout
:
~/elf_injector $ ./elf_injector test chunks/startup_dump_strip.bin 112
inserted 280 byte thunk at pos 1484, start 0x678
inserted 1600 byte chunk at pos 1764, start 0x754
~/elf_injector $ ./test.injected
Arguments:
./test.injected
Environment:
INSIDE_EMACS=28.2,comint,tramp:2.5.3.28.2
SSH_CLIENT=192.168.1.2 33816 22
TEXTDOMAIN=Linux-PAM
XDG_SESSION_TYPE=tty
SHLVL=0
MOTD_SHOWN=pam
...
LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
SSH_CONNECTION=192.168.1.2 33816 192.168.1.12 22
TERMCAP=
TMOUT=0
Auxiliary Vector:
16:33238(0x81d6)
6:4096(0x1000)
17:100(0x64)
...
26:0(0x0)
31:3204018156(0xbef96fec)
15:3204017368(0xbef96cd8)
Inject Info:
1:1764(0x6e4)
2:1600(0x640)
3:112(0x70)
Testing 123...
~/elf_injector $
inject_info
is non-standard and is introduced by the
elf_injector
as a way of passing along information to the injected chunk..  It's defined as an array of:
struct inject_info
{
unsigned int type;
unsigned int val;
};
The supported types are:
#define II_NULL            0
#define II_CNK_POS         1
#define II_CNK_LEN         2
#define II_CNK_ENT_OFF     3
The value of
II_CNK_POS
is the position in bytes of the start of the
chunk
in the running executable's file, the value of
II_CNK_LEN
is the length in bytes of the
chunk
, and the value of
II_CNK_ENT_OFF
is the offset in bytes from the beginning of the
chunk
from which to start execution.
The final element in
inject_info
array will have a type of
II_NULL
.
copy_chunk
copy_chunk
picks a random executable (that has not yet been injected) in the current working directory, injects itself into the executable, and prints the name of the executable to
stdout
:
~/elf_injector $ ./elf_injector test ./chunks/copy_chunk_strip.bin 1640
inserted 280 byte thunk at pos 1

主要讨论点：RPI Pico（RP2040）及其新版本RP2350的性能、优缺点以及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [donperignon] 认为RPI Pico（RP2040）作为MCU表现优秀，开发工具和文档齐全，开发过程流畅，尤其是PIO功能潜力巨大。然而，由于在集成SD卡时遇到问题，最终回到了STM32的开发。总体上仍看好RP2040，特别是其PIO和未来RISCV核心的潜力。

• [zdw] 关注RP2040的I/O 5V耐压特性，认为这是一个很好的补充功能。

• [bluehex] 赞赏Raspberry Pi快速解决已知问题，并在一年内发布了新的 stepping，认为这种响应速度值得肯定。

• [tverbeure] 提到RP2040已被正式宣布支持200 MHz，期待RP2350也能达到同样的频率，目前仅支持150 MHz。

• [AlexeyBrin] 提醒在5V电压应用于GPIO时，需确保VDDIO供电，否则可能损坏芯片，强调阅读更新后的数据手册的重要性。

• [kpcyrd] 喜欢使用rp2040-zero进行嵌入式Rust项目开发，但由于rp2350 mini zero的成本较高，暂时会继续使用rp2040-zero，期待rp2350价格下降后再切换。

• [mallets] 计划围绕RP2040开发新应用，并可能在未来十年或更长时间内继续使用，前提是发布兼容的继任者。

• [irdc] 指出新的stepping修复了著名的E9 erratum，解决了GPIO异常行为的问题。

• [puzzlingcaptcha] 担心Raspberry Pi未能及时沟通新stepping的开发，可能导致最近购买的A2-stepping设备被淘汰和浪费。

补充讨论：
• 对RP2040和RP2350的性能和频率的讨论。
• 对RP2040新stepping修复已知问题的赞赏。
• 对RP2040 I/O 5V耐压功能的关注。
• 对成本和性价比的考虑，特别是rp2350和rp2040-zero之间的价格差异。
• 对Raspberry Pi沟通不及时可能导致设备浪费的担忧。

data.title: Do variable names matter for AI code completion? (2025)
data.author: yakubov_org
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了变量名称对AI代码补全的影响。通过实验测试了8种AI模型在500个Python代码样本上的表现，样本使用了7种不同的命名风格，包括描述性名称（如`current_temperature`）、标准风格（如`snake_case`）、简化名称（如`calc_pay`）和混淆名称（如`fn2`）。结果显示，描述性变量名称能显著提高代码补全的准确性。具体发现包括：描述性名称的完全匹配率为34.2%，而混淆名称为16.6%；其语义相似性也更高。实验表明，清晰的变量名称不仅有利于人类阅读，也能提升AI代码补全的效果，尽管它们使用更多 tokens。不同模型架构下结果一致，描述性名称表现最佳。因此，使用AI编码工具时，建议采用描述性变量名称以获得更好补全效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：变量命名对AI代码补全的影响以及变量命名在编程实践中的重要性

不同观点：
• Groxx认为，开发者过度重视变量命名，尤其是在处理类似数组的数据结构时，命名并没有实际意义，反而容易出错。他指出，程序员在命名上的一致性可能导致了这种过度重视。
• yakubov_org通过实验表明，描述性强的变量名（如"current_temperature"）确实对AI代码补全有帮助，并提供了研究论文作为证据。
• k__幽默地指出，良好的编码实践因为AI的应用才被重视，而不是因为人类程序员。
• nemo1618建议重新使用匈牙利命名法，认为这种命名法可以为大型语言模型（LLM）提供帮助，因为可以直接看到变量类型。
• ssalka支持使用具有语义的变量名，认为这对于LLM理解和使用变量至关重要，除非在竞赛编程中。
• r0s强调代码的主要读者仍然是人类，因此可读性至关重要，直到AI能直接编译成机器语言。
• quuxplusone对yakubov_org的研究方法提出质疑，认为研究没有明确区分不同命名风格对模型的具体影响，并指出需要更细致的研究。
• Sohcahtoa82提出有趣的建议，希望看到对抗性变量名的实验，即故意使用误导性的变量名，观察其对AI的影响。
• robertclaus对实际数据的展示表示赞赏。
• OutOfHere认为，长函数中的注释和明确的类型标注对代码可读性和LLM的正确理解有帮助。
• qwertytyyuu对SCREAM_SNAKE_CASE命名的优越表现表示不解和幽默。

补充讨论：
• 变量命名对AI代码补全的影响需要更多细化的研究和数据支持。
• 不同命名风格和注释对人类和AI的理解都有不同的影响，值得进一步探讨。
• 编码实践在AI时代可能需要重新审视和调整，以平衡人类和机器的需求。

44689778.article_content:
Do Variable Names Matter for AI Code Completion?
When GitHub Copilot suggests your next line of code, does it matter whether your variables are named
current_temperature
or just
x
?
I ran an experiment to find out, testing 8 different AI models on 500 Python code samples across 7 naming styles. The results suggest that descriptive variable names do help AI code completion.
The Experiment
Each code sample was transformed into different naming conventions:
Descriptive (
process_user_input
)
Standard styles (snake_case, PascalCase, SCREAM_SNAKE_CASE)
Minimal (
calc_pay
)
Obfuscated (
fn2
)
Models ranging from 0.5B to 8B parameters completed 25 tokens for each sample. I measured exact matches, Levenshtein similarity (edit distance) and semantic correctness using an LLM judge.
Key Findings
Descriptive names performed best across all models:
34.2% exact match rate vs 16.6% for obfuscated names
0.786 Levenshtein similarity vs 0.666 for obfuscated names
0.874 semantic similarity vs 0.802 for obfuscated
Performance across naming schemes shows consistent patterns
The ranking was consistent: descriptive > SCREAM_SNAKE_CASE > snake_case > PascalCase > minimal > obfuscated.
Descriptive names use 41% more tokens but achieve 8.9% better semantic performance, suggesting AI models prioritize clarity over compression.
Despite using more tokens, descriptive names achieve better performance
For Developers
If you're using AI coding tools, descriptive variable names appear to provide better completions. The improvement is measurable.
This aligns with existing guidance for human readability - it turns out clear names benefit AI systems too.
Cross-model consistency shows these patterns hold across different architectures
Full paper
:
Variable Naming Impact on AI Code Completion: An Empirical Study

data.title: 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey Results
data.author: colingw
data.article_summary: 文章主要总结了2025年开发者对AI工具和技术的态度与趋势。OpenAI的GPT模型在最受赞赏和期望的AI模型中居首，而Anthropic的Claude Sonnet模型在期望和赞赏度上紧随其后。然而，多数开发者对AI工具的准确性持怀疑态度，不信任的比例（46%）高于信任（33%）。此外，2025年对AI工具的正面 sentiment 有所下降，从之前的70%以上降至60%。在云开发和协作工具方面，Cargo成为最受赞赏的工具，GitHub则取代Jira成为最受期望的协作工具。开发者放弃某项技术的主要原因包括隐私问题、高昂定价和更好替代品的出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stack Overflow 开发者调查结果的代表性和网站用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [chistev] 认为Windows在调查中占主导地位，但实际讨论中Mac似乎更普遍。他还抱怨了网站上的"接受cookies"弹窗过大，影响了使用，并且找不到拒绝所有cookies的选项。

• [colingw] 指出调查中缺少一些特定的编辑器（如Emacs）和编程语言（如Clojure），暗示调查设计可能存在偏见或遗漏。

• [ChrisRR] 认为调查结果被学生和初级开发者所主导，导致其无法准确反映整个行业的现状。

补充讨论：
• 关于Windows和Mac在开发者中的实际使用情况存在认知差异，虽然调查显示Windows占主导，但一些人认为Mac在实际开发环境中更普遍。

• 用户对网站用户体验问题（如cookies弹窗）表示不满，特别是当缺少明显的拒绝选项时，影响了用户的自主选择权。

• 对调查的设计和参与者构成的质疑反映了调查结果的可靠性和代表性问题，尤其是涉及行业趋势时。

争议焦点：
• 调查结果是否能够真实反映开发者群体的多样性和实际使用习惯，尤其是在编辑器和编程语言的选择上。

• 网站用户体验问题，特别是cookies弹窗的设计，是否对用户造成了不必要的干扰和不便。

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了使用Zig语言实现的数独求解器，并通过 dancing-links (DLX) 算法进行优化。DLX算法是一种解决“精确覆盖”问题的高效回溯算法，通过0和1组成的矩阵来表示问题和部分解。具体到数独问题，矩阵需要满足行、列、九宫格及单元格的唯一性约束，总共有4×9×9个约束条件。文章详细描述了如何将数独问题转换为精确覆盖问题，并通过选择满足约束的行来逐步求解。

初始实现中，每次需要新单元格时都调用`allocator.create()`，导致不必要的性能开销。通过一次性分配四个单元格（每 puzzle 约750次分配），显著提高了性能，使求解时间平均减少到1毫秒。文章还提到，对于标准9x9数独，稀疏矩阵并非空间高效，建议使用索引替代64位指针以节省空间。

44695385.article_content:
Optimi-Zi(n)g Sudoku-Solving
26 July 2025
, in
Olivier's log
One of the first program that I wrote in Zig (in September 2023) was a Sudoku-Solver, implementing the dancing-links (DLX) algorithm. I decided to revisit this program recently to experiment with benchmarking and try to increase its speed.
Dancing-Links (DLX) algorithm applied to sudoku
The Dancing-Links algorithm is an efficient backtracking algorithm to solve "exact-cover" problems, by using a matrix of 0 and 1s.
Dancing Links on Wikipedia
In an exact-cover problem, there is a bunch of constraints (modelled as columns of a matrix) and many partial solutions (modelled as lines of a matrix). The goal is to pick some solutions, so that all constraints are met exactly once. In the matrix-modelisation a 1 in a cell means that this partial solution meets the given constraint. Solving the exact-cover problem transposes to selecting rows, so that each column as exactly one 1 in it.
To convert a sudoku to an exact-cover problem, we generate 4*9*9 columns to represent the following constraints:
a given number must appear exactly once in each sudoku-row (9*9 constraints)
a given number must appear exactly once in each sudoku-column (9*9 constraints)
a given number must appear exactly once in each 3*3-block (9*9 constraints)
there must be a number in each sudoku-cell (9*9 cells)
Assigning a number to a sudoku-cell satisfies exactly 4 constraints. For instance putting a 1 in the top-left sudoku-cell satisfies:
the need for a 1 in the topmost row
the need for a 1 in the leftmost column
the need for a 1 in the top-left 3*3-block
the need for a number in the top-left cell
Since there are 81 cells we get 9*81 lines with exactly 4 1s per line.
Out of the 236.196 cells only 2.916 are 1s (sparse-matrix). Instead of having the whole matrix in memory, only the "1-cell" are instanciated, with a pointer to its "neighbors" (top, right, bottom, left).
Doing some napkin-math, the whole-matrix as bit-set array should take about 29KB of space. Using 4*64-bits pointers in the sparse version takes more than 3 times the space (~92KB). So for the standard 9*9 sudoku, the sparse matrix is not space-efficient. Maybe the space-usage could be improved by using indexes instead of 64-bits pointers?
At the beginning some cells already have assigned values, so we know that those lines must be part of the solution. Selecting a line for a solution means that its 4 constraints are met and that all other lines which have 1s in common columns with the selected line must be ignored. In the example above of the 1 in the top-left cell, we must now ignore:
all other 8 lines which set a 1 in the topmost row somewhere else
all other 8 lines which set a 1 in the leftmost column somewhere else
all other 8 lines which set a 1 in the top-left 3*3-block somewhere else (note that some of those lines were also matched by the previous descriptions)
all other 8 lines which set a number in the top-left cell
Solving the whole exact-cover problem corresponds to selecting lines until all constraints are met.
If a constraint cannot be met because all lines are already ignored, it means that there is no solution (so we likely made a wrong choice some steps earlier).
We now have the steps to solve any puzzle!
1. Setup the matrix, with all constraints (columns) and partial solutions (lines)
2. Select the pre-filled lines (its constraints are met and the other lines are ignored)
3. If all constraints are satisfied, SUCCESS! (return true)
4. Of the unsatisfied constraints, take the one with the fewest 1s.
5. If there is a constraint without any 1, FAILURE (return false to backtrack)
6. Otherwise consider this constraint met and loop over the lines with a 1:
a) Consider the line to be part of the solution
b) Ignore the other lines which have a 1 in common in any column with the current line
c) Call 3. recursively. On failure, undo b) and try with the next line in a)
d) If no line was suitable, FAILURE (return false to backtrack)
And this is how the whole implementation is done. The sudoku solver instanciates a DLX solver with the right number of columns, adds all partial solutions as lines, select the solutions corresponding to the pre-filled cells and calls the `solve` method. The list of partial solutions can then be translated back to sudoku cells before returning.
Optimizing allocations
Unfortunately I realized far too late that proper benchmarking needs a stable representative input corpus and precise tools (like hyperfine or poop).
Not being used to manually manage memory allocations (Go, Python, JavaScript, PHP... plenty of options!), I initially called `allocator.create()` for each needed cell (using an arena to deallocate them all at once at the end). It turns out that allocating 3000 times is reasonbally fast and the program was able to solve puzzles in 1ms on average.
A simple optimization consisted in allocating all the 4 cells of a line at once (so about 750 allocations per puzzle). This brought a nice

data.title: Ask HN: How will the OSA affect small Mastodon instances?
data.author: Digit-Al
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国《在线安全法》（OSA）对Mastodon等小型服务提供者的影响和要求

不同观点：
• [edent] 认为，根据Ofcom的规定，用户数少于700万的服务在英国被视为"较小"服务，因此要求较为宽松。对于Mastodon这样的去中心化平台，如果允许未经审核的通信，可能会有更高的风险。不过，大多数要求（如回应投诉、行为守则、设置管理员、使用CDN过滤儿童不良内容等）都是Mastodon服务应该做的基本措施。如果只是为自己托管服务，没有其他用户，则无需担心合规问题。

• [PaulRobinson] 认为，英国政府短期内不会广泛解读和实施该法律。如果Mastodon实例的月活跃用户（MAUs）少于300万，通常没有问题，但一旦涉及托管《在线安全法》旨在保护未成年人免受的有害内容，该实例将面临严格调查，可能需要实施年龄验证或关闭实例，甚至可能诉诸法庭。风险在于托管此类内容的可能性，而不是仅看影响。如果只是为熟人提供服务，问题不大；但若涉及儿童访问，则会引发更多问题。

• [1over137] 仅仅澄清了OSA代表《英国在线安全法》，没有深入讨论影响。

• [runjake] 认为Mastodon作为一个较为小众且非企业化的平台，不太会受到《在线安全法》的实质影响。

补充讨论：
• [cornfieldlabs] 提到了在其他平台上询问了一个相关问题，但没有具体展开讨论内容。

争议焦点：
• Mastodon实例在何种情况下会触发《在线安全法》的严格调查和处理，尤其是涉及托管有害内容时的法律风险。
• 对于小型服务提供者，如何平衡合规要求和实际操作的可行性，尤其是在用户数量和内容审核方面。

总结：讨论围绕Mastodon等小型服务在《在线安全法》下的合规要求展开，特别是用户数量、内容审核和法律风险等方面。不同观点主要集中在法律的实际影响程度和Mastodon实例的运营风险上。

data.title: Meta Is Going to Let Job Candidates Use AI During Coding Tests
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Meta宣布，将允许部分编码岗位的求职者在面试中使用AI助手，并邀请现有员工参与模拟AI辅助面试，以帮助完善面试流程。此举反映出硅谷巨头正推动软件工程师在工作中使用AI，并倾向于 hiring 能够与AI协作的员工。Meta CEO扎克伯格曾表示，预计AI将能够胜任中级工程师的工作，并最终承担大量代码编写任务。不过，一些公司如Anthropic禁止求职者在面试中使用AI，而某些AI工具则声称可以帮助求职者秘密使用AI。整体而言，这一话题在硅谷引发了争议，一些工程师担心新一代程序员可能更依赖AI提示而非实际编程能力。

44723289.article_content:
Save Story
Save this story
Save Story
Save this story
Meta told employees
that it is going to allow some coding job candidates to use an AI assistant during the interview process, according to internal Meta communications seen by 404 Media. The company has also asked existing employees to volunteer for a “mock AI-enabled interview,” the messages say.
It’s the latest indication that Silicon Valley giants are pushing software engineers to use AI in their jobs, and it signals a broader move toward hiring employees who can vibecode as part of their jobs.
“AI-Enabled Interviews—Call for Mock Candidates,” a post from earlier this month on an internal Meta message board reads. “Meta is developing a new type of coding interview in which candidates have access to an AI assistant. This is more representative of the developer environment that our future employees will work in, and also makes LLM-based cheating less effective.”
“We need mock candidates,” the post continues. “If you would like to experience a mock AI-enabled interview, please sign up in this sheet. The questions are still in development; data from you will help shape the future of interviewing at Meta.”
This article was created in partnership with
404
Media
, a journalist-owned publication covering how technology impacts humans. For more stories like this,
sign up here
.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has made clear at numerous all-hands and in public podcast interviews that he is not just pushing the company’s software engineers towards using AI in their work, but that he foresees human beings managing “AI coding agents” that will write code for the company.
“I think this year, probably in 2025, we at Meta as well as the other companies that are basically working on this, are going to have an AI that can effectively be a midlevel engineer that you have at your company that can write code,” Zuckerberg
told Joe Rogan in January
. “Over time we’ll get to a point where a lot of the code in our apps and including the AI that we generate is actually going to be built by AI engineers instead of people engineers … In the future people are going to be so much more creative, and they’re going to be freed up to do kind of crazy things.”
In April, Zuckerberg expanded on this slightly on a
podcast with Dwarkesh Patel
, where he said that “sometime in the next 12 to 18 months, we’ll reach the point where most of the code that’s going towards [AI] efforts is written by AI.”
While it’s true that many tech companies have pushed software engineers to use AI in their work, they have been slower to allow new applicants to use AI during the interview process. In fact, Anthropic, which makes the AI tool Claude, has specifically told job applicants that they
cannot use AI during the interview process
. To circumvent that type of ban, some AI tools promise to allow applicants to
secretly use AI during coding interviews
. The topic, in general, has been a controversial one in Silicon Valley. Established software engineers worry that the next batch of coders will be more AI “prompters” and “vibecoders” than software engineers, and that they may not know how to
troubleshoot AI-written code
when something goes wrong.
“We're obviously focused on using AI to help engineers with their day-to-day work, so it should be no surprise that we're testing how to provide these tools to applicants during interviews,” a Meta spokesperson told 404 Media.

data.title: RP2350 E9 GPIO erratum fixed in new A4 stepping
data.author: theodote
data.article_summary: Raspberry Pi发布了RP2350微控制器的新版本——A4 stepping，修复了多个漏洞和安全问题，包括E9 GPIO错误以及在2024年黑客挑战中发现的glitching bugs。RP2350A和RP2350B变种将更新为RP2350A0A4和RP2350B0A4。同时，RP2354A和RP2354B变种配备2MB闪存，无需板载闪存。新版本兼容pico-sdk 2.1.0及以上版本，并推出了pico-sdk 2.2.0，包含多个bug修复、文档改进和新功能，如强化AES解密代码和支持自解密二进制文件。此外，Raspberry Pi宣布了RP2350 Hacking Challenge 2，鼓励发现新的安全漏洞。最后，公布了多款微控制器的单单元及批量价格。

44722997.article_content:
The
Raspberry Pi RP2350
dual-core Arm/RISC-V has gotten a new version –
A4 stepping
– addressing bugs and security vulnerabilities, notably the infamous E9 GPIO erratum and glitching bugs in the A2 stepping identified by the 2024 Hacking Challenge.
Both RP2350A and RP2350B variants will benefit from the new stepping and be marked RP2350A0A4 and RP2350B0A4, respectively. The company also announced the availability of the 2MB flash variants, the RP2354A and RP2354B (
unveiled in March 2025
), that do not require flash on the board.
Raspberry Pi RP2350A A4 stepping
RP2350 A4 stepping highlights:
Fixes
Glitching bugs
identified in the 2024 Hacking Challenge
. Exploits required physical access to the chip.
The E9 GPIO erratum related to GPIO pull-ups.
A4 stepping is a drop-in replacement for the earlier A2 stepping.
5V-tolerant GPIOs; Note: the chip must remain powered while 5V IOs are used (See updated
datasheet
for details)
RP2354A and RP2354B variants with 2MB of stacked-in-package QSPI flash
E9 GPIO Erratum Fix (A2 vs A4)
RP2350 naming convention explains why RP2354 has 2MB flash (and not 4MB flash)
An important note is that the new A4 stepping of the RP2350 microcontrollers will only work with version 2.1.0 or later of the pico-sdk, so make sure your firmware is updated to support the new versions of the MCU.
While on the subject of software support, Raspberry Pi also introduced
version 2.2.0 of pico-sdk
, pico-examples, and picotool with:
Various bug fixes, documentation improvements, and new features.
Hardened AES decryption code with high resistance against side-channel attacks.
Support for self-decrypting binaries (AES encryption). The encrypted binary will embed a bootloader that will decrypt your code/data to RAM before running.
New Raspberry Pi RP2350 examples for encryption, OTA (over-the-air) update, and UART bootloading.
Raspberry Pi RP2350B A4 stepping
Since security is always evolving, the company also announced the
RP2350 Hacking Challenge 2
. This follows the 2024 RP2350 Hacking Challenge, where several security bugs were found and fixed in the A4 stepping. The British company believes its new hardened AES implementation is resistant to side-channel attacks (SCA), and challenges people to prove them wrong.
The company also released price information for all variants of the RP2040 and RP2350 microcontrollers.

data.author: obscurette

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：挪威及美国的富裕经济体中出现的经济和社会问题，包括基础设施支出、社会福利、生产力下降等。

不同观点：
• **美国基础设施浪费问题**：MontyCarloHall指出美国的基础设施建设成本远高于其他发达国家，如纽约第二大道地铁延长线的建设成本比巴黎高出数倍。美国的高速铁路项目成本也远超其他国家，显示出极端的浪费现象。这种浪费不仅限于公共支出，还包括私人建设。

• **挪威是否面临严重问题**：
   - **Vinnl**认为挪威出现的问题（如病假增加、学生成绩下降、浪费性基建项目）并不值得大惊小怪，只是一些值得关注的小问题，且每个国家都可能存在类似问题。
   - **Workaccount2**则认为挪威正面临“信托基金综合症”的风险，即由于富裕而导致无节制的浪费性支出和缺乏方向感，挪威可能会像一些富裕家庭一样挥霍其财富。
   - **physarum_salad**反驳称挪威整体表现良好，提出的问题只是富裕国家常见的“奢侈抱怨”，并引用了挪威专家对相关批评的反驳。

• **挪威社会老龄化与社会福利问题**：megaman821指出挪威未来将面临老龄化人口问题，如何在维持慷慨的社会福利的同时应对这一挑战值得关注。挪威可能成为其他国家应对老龄化的蓝图或警示。

• **挪威是否应追求更多财富**：
   - **Ragnarork**质疑追逐更多财富的必要性，认为挪威选择不疯狂追求财富是合理的，并指出对挪威的批评可能源于其财富未流向外界。
   - **amelius**提出是否有其他更典型的富裕石油国家可供讨论。

• **资本主义与民主制度的批判**：
   - **dostick**对资本主义和民主制度进行了深刻批判，认为两者都是未经审查和更新的有缺陷系统，并呼吁研究和设计新的社会经济体系。
   - **bparsons**则指出媒体评论中普遍存在的“经济新闻即坏新闻”现象，认为对挪威的批评可能只是这种倾向的反映。

补充讨论：
• **挪威信托基金的使用与管理**：HardCodedBias认为挪威的主权财富基金为每个人提供了很好的起点，并建议加强对政府从基金中提款的规则。

• **COVID-19的影响**：StevenWaterman指出挪威病假增加和学生成绩下降可能与COVID-19大流行有关，而非仅仅是富裕带来的问题。

争议焦点：挪威是否真的面临严重的经济和社会问题，或者这些只是富裕国家常见的“奢侈抱怨”。此外，关于资本主义和民主制度的缺陷及是否应研究和设计新的社会经济体系也存在讨论。

   - **bparsons**则指出媒体评论中普遍存在的“经济新闻即坏新闻”现象，认为对挪威的批评可能只是这种倾向的反映。

补充讨论：
• **挪威信托基金的使用与管理**：HardCodedBias认为挪威的主权财富基金为每个人提供了很好的起点，并建议加强对政府从基金中提款的规则。

• **COVID-19的影响**：StevenWaterman指出挪威病假增加和学生成绩下降可能与COVID-19大流行有关，而非仅仅是富裕带来的问题。

争议焦点：挪威是否真的面临严重的经济和社会问题，或者这些只是富裕国家常见的“奢侈抱怨”。此外，关于资本主义和民主制度的缺陷及是否应研究和设计新的社会经济体系也存在讨论。

(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41557-025-01867-z
Ammonia (NH
3
) is vital for agriculture, as it is the basis for fertilizers that are needed to feed the world's population. Currently, ammonia is mostly produced by the Haber-Bosch process, which turns nitrogen gas (N
2
) from the air into ammonia. The problem is that this process requires enormous amounts of energy while generating significant gas emissions.
Scientists have long searched for more efficient and environmentally friendly ways to produce ammonia. Nature does this efficiently through enzymes called nitrogenases, but replicating these
biological processes
on an industrial scale has proven challenging.
"All
molecular catalysts
developed so far typically attach nitrogen molecules—which are composed of two
nitrogen atoms
bonded together—to a single metal center in a linear, 'end-on' arrangement. It means that one nitrogen molecule binds only one metal, via one of its two atoms," says Professor Marinella Mazzanti at EPFL.
"In contrast, nature uses a multimetallic approach, where nitrogen molecules bind to more than one metal. It has been proposed that the nitrogen binds in a 'side on' way, meaning both nitrogen atoms bind two metals, making it easier to break their strong bonds."
Inspired by nature
Now, a team led by Mazzanti has developed the first molecular uranium catalyst that can bind
nitrogen gas
in a similar "side-on" way and convert it into ammonia.
The work, appearing in
Nature Chemistry
, reveals a new catalytic pathway, bridging biological efficiency and industrial feasibility, and opening doors for more sustainable ammonia production methods.
The scientists built a special molecule using uranium combined with a triamidoamine ligand, producing a molecular complex that can hold nitrogen gas (N
2
) sideways.
They then progressively reduced the nitrogen gas by adding electrons step-by-step, breaking the powerful bond between the gas's two nitrogen atoms.
The researchers carefully studied and isolated various stages of this reduction process, creating intermediate molecules (nitrogen forms like N
2
2-
, N
2
3-
, and N
2
4-
) until finally splitting nitrogen completely into two separate nitride ions (N
3-
).
A different way to make ammonia differently
Their experiments showed the uranium complex could run repeatedly in a cycle, effectively turning nitrogen gas into ammonia multiple times; specifically, up to 8.8 equivalents of ammonia per uranium catalyst. This demonstrated for the first time that side-on nitrogen binding—a likely binding mode in nature's enzymes—can provide a viable route for producing ammonia.
The catalyst clarifies previously unknown steps in nitrogen conversion chemistry and shows that uranium, historically among the first metals used industrially to make ammonia, still holds untapped potential.
This discovery provides crucial insights into nitrogen chemistry and shows how
uranium
-based systems can offer new avenues for future
ammonia
production technologies.

data.title: Union Pacific to buy Norfolk in $85B mega U.S. railroad deal
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: Union Pacific宣布将以850亿美元收购其较小的竞争对手Norfolk Southern，以打造美国首个横跨东西海岸的货运铁路运营商。此交易若获批，将合并Union Pacific在美西三分之二地区的优势与Norfolk的19,500英里东部网络，重塑全国货物运输格局。这将是该行业史上最大收购案，面临诸多监管障碍，尤其是反垄断审查。美国 Surface Transportation Board 自2025年初采取更为行业友好的并购审查方式，主席Patrick Fuchs支持加快审核。此次合并还需获得工会支持，并可能引发其他联邦机构审查。主要铁路工会反对合并，担心影响就业和铁路服务。此次交易也促使BNSF和CSX等竞争对手考虑合并选项。此前，加拿大太平洋铁路与Kansas City Southern的31亿美元合并案在2023年获批，尽管遭遇监管阻力。

Union Pacific to buy Norfolk Southern in $85 billion deal
Squawk Box
Union Pacific
said on Tuesday it would buy smaller rival
Norfolk Southern
in an $85 billion deal, to create the nation's first coast-to-coast freight rail operator and reshape the movement of goods from grains to autos across the country.
If approved, the deal would combine Union Pacific's stronghold in the western two-thirds of the U.S. with Norfolk's 19,500-mile network that primarily spans 22 eastern states.
This would mark the largest-ever buyout in the sector, merging Union Pacific, the biggest U.S. railroad operator, with Norfolk, one of the top players, granting the combined company transcontinental dominance.
On Thursday, the two companies had said they were in advanced discussion for a possible merger.
The transaction faces numerous regulatory hurdles and will serve as a key test of the changed thinking around antitrust issues under President Donald Trump.
Since early 2025, the U.S. Surface Transportation Board, the federal regulatory agency overseeing railroads, has signaled a more industry-friendly approach to merger reviews.
Chairman Patrick Fuchs, appointed to the post in January by Trump, has advocated for faster timelines for preliminary assessments, a greater focus on competitive balance rather than blocking consolidation, and a willingness to enforce conditions post-merger rather than deny deals preemptively.
The talks have also prompted competitors BNSF, owned by
Berkshire Hathaway
, and CSX to explore merger options, people familiar with the matter said.
Union Pacific's deal for Norfolk would also need support from labor unions and could invite scrutiny from several other federal agencies.
Major railroad unions have long opposed consolidation, arguing that such mergers threaten jobs and risk disrupting rail service.
The North American rail industry has been grappling with volatile freight volumes, rising labor and fuel costs, and growing pressure from shippers over service reliability, factors that could further complicate the merger.
The last major deal in the industry was the $31 billion merger of Canadian Pacific and Kansas City Southern, which created the first and only single-line rail network connecting Canada, the U.S., and Mexico.
That deal, finalized in 2023, faced heavy regulatory resistance over fears it would curb competition, cut jobs, and disrupt service, but it was ultimately approved.

data.title: Iron Law of Oligarchy
data.author: rzk
data.article_summary: 罗伯特·米歇尔斯提出的“寡头铁律”理论认为，任何民主组织最终都会演变为由少数精英统治的寡头制度。这是由于组织的复杂性和规模要求决策权集中于少数领导成员，以维持效率。这些领导层通过控制信息和决策程序来巩固权力，导致普通成员难以参与决策。米歇尔斯观察到，即使是标榜民主的政党和工会也无法避免这种趋势。他总结道：“谁说组织，谁就说寡头。”这一理论强调，官僚化必然导致权力集中，而权力则会腐化领导者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于组织中直接民主的可行性以及精英阶层在各种制度中的出现和影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：技术进步使直接民主成为可能。评论者"since no sufficiently large and complex organization can function purely as a direct democracy"认为，由于技术进步，直接民主的技术障碍已不存在，可以通过技术实现大规模的直接民主投票。

• 观点二：结构性问题导致权力集中。评论者"jcalx"引用《无结构的暴政》一文，指出即使在非正式组织中，权力也会因为必要性、便利性以及非正式网络等原因集中，暗示直接民主可能无法避免结构性问题带来的权力集中。

• 观点三：精英阶层的普遍存在。评论者"SilverElfin"质疑直接民主理论的局限性，认为精英阶层不仅在民主制度中会出现，在任何人群组织中都会出现，暗示任何制度都难以避免精英阶层的出现。

• 观点四：精英主义的制度化。评论者"mbones"提到法西斯意大利的一个机构，其核心理念是精英相对于普通民众的优越性，强调精英拥有更高的智力和技能，而普通民众则缺乏自治能力，因此需要精英治理。

• 观点五：小单位竞争是解决寡头统治的途径。评论者"recursivedoubts"认为寡头统治是人类系统的自然状态，建议通过小单位的竞争（如国家、公司等）来制约寡头统治，但指出这种设计在当今世界并不受欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 评论者"jcalx"提供了一个参考链接，指向《无结构的暴政》一文，以支持其关于权力集中问题的论点。
• 评论者"recursivedoubts"进一步讨论了寡头统治的普遍性，并提出通过小单位竞争来限制寡头权力的系统设计思路，同时指出这种思路在当今世界并不流行。

争议焦点：
• 直接民主的技术可行性与结构性问题之间的争议。
• 精英阶层在各种制度中的不可避免性及其影响。
• 小单位竞争作为制约寡头统治的可行性与现实性。

The
iron law of oligarchy
is a
political theory
first developed by the German-born Italian
sociologist
Robert Michels
in his 1911 book
Political Parties
.
[
1
]
It asserts that rule by an elite, or
oligarchy
, is inevitable as an "iron law" within any
democratic
organization as part of the "tactical and technical necessities" of the organization.
[
1
]
Michels' theory states that all complex organizations, regardless of how democratic they are when started, eventually develop into oligarchies. Michels observed that since no sufficiently large and complex organization can function purely as a
direct democracy
,
power
within an organization will always get delegated to individuals within that group, elected or otherwise. As he put it in
Political Parties
, "It is organization which gives dominion of the elected over the electors. [...] Who says organization, says oligarchy."
[
2
]
According to Michels, all organizations eventually come to be run by a leadership class who often function as paid
administrators
,
executives
,
spokespersons
, or
political strategists
for the organization. Far from being servants of the masses, Michels argues, this leadership class, rather than the organization's membership, will inevitably grow to dominate the organization's
power structures
.
[
3
]
By controlling who has access to information, those in power can
centralize
their power, often with little accountability, due to the
apathy
,
indifference
, and non-participation most rank-and-file members have in relation to their organization's decision-making processes.
[
citation needed
]
Democratic attempts to hold leadership positions
accountable
are prone to fail, since with power comes the ability to reward
loyalty
, the ability to control information about the organization, and the ability to control what procedures the organization follows when making decisions.
All of these mechanisms can be used to strongly influence the outcome of any decisions made "democratically" by members.
[
4
]
In 1911, using
anecdotes
from the histories of
political parties
and
trade unions
struggling to operate democratically, Michels applied his argument to
representative democracy
at large.
[
1
]
He believed that "[h]istorical evolution mocks all the prophylactic measures that have been adopted for the prevention of oligarchy."
[
5
]
[
1
]
History
[
edit
]
In 1911, Robert Michels argued that the socialist parties of Europe, despite their democratic ideology and provisions for mass participation, seemed to be dominated by their leaders just like traditional
conservative
parties. Michels' conclusion was that the problem lay in the nature of organizations. The more
liberal
and democratic modern era allowed the formation of organizations with novel and revolutionary goals, but as such organizations become more complex, they became less and less democratic and revolutionary. Michels formulated the "iron law of oligarchy": "Who says organization, says oligarchy."
[
6
]
He later became an important ideologue of
Benito Mussolini
's
fascist
regime in Italy, teaching economics at the
University of Perugia
.
[
7
]
[
8
]
Reasons
[
edit
]
"Organization implies the tendency to oligarchy. In every organization, whether it be a political party, a professional union, or any other association of the kind, the aristocratic tendency manifests itself very clearly. The mechanism of the organization, while conferring a solidity of structure, induces serious changes in the organized mass, completely inverting the respective position of the leaders and the led. As a result of organization, every party of professional union becomes divided into a minority of directors and a majority of directed."
— Robert Michels
[
9
]
Michels stressed several factors that underlie the iron law of oligarchy. Darcy K. Leach summarized them briefly as: "Bureaucracy happens. If bureaucracy happens, power rises. Power corrupts."
[
6
]
Any large organization, Michels pointed out, has to create a
bureaucracy
to maintain its efficiency as it becomes larger—many decisions have to be made daily that cannot be made by large numbers of disorganized people. For the organization to function, centralization has to occur and power will end up in the hands of a few. Those few—the oligarchy—will use all means necessary to preserve and further increase their power.
[
6
]

• 观点三：精英阶层的普遍存在。评论者"SilverElfin"质疑直接民主理论的局限性，认为精英阶层不仅在民主制度中会出现，在任何人群组织中都会出现，暗示任何制度都难以避免精英阶层的出现。

• 观点四：精英主义的制度化。评论者"mbones"提到法西斯意大利的一个机构，其核心理念是精英相对于普通民众的优越性，强调精英拥有更高的智力和技能，而普通民众则缺乏自治能力，因此需要精英治理。

• 观点五：小单位竞争是解决寡头统治的途径。评论者"recursivedoubts"认为寡头统治是人类系统的自然状态，建议通过小单位的竞争（如国家、公司等）来制约寡头统治，但指出这种设计在当今世界并不受欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 评论者"jcalx"提供了一个参考链接，指向《无结构的暴政》一文，以支持其关于权力集中问题的论点。
• 评论者"recursivedoubts"进一步讨论了寡头统治的普遍性，并提出通过小单位竞争来限制寡头权力的系统设计思路，同时指出这种思路在当今世界并不流行。

争议焦点：
• 直接民主的技术可行性与结构性问题之间的争议。
• 精英阶层在各种制度中的不可避免性及其影响。
• 小单位竞争作为制约寡头统治的可行性与现实性。

Anthropic Faces Potentially “Business-Ending” Copyright Lawsuit
A class action over pirated books exposes the 'responsible' AI company to penalties that could bankrupt it — and reshape the entire industry
Garrison Lovely

CEO Dario Amodei at TechCrunch Disrupt 2023
This piece has been updated to add additional context and clarify some details.
Anthropic, the AI startup that’s long presented itself as the industry’s safe and ethical choice, is now facing legal penalties that could bankrupt the company. Damages resulting from its mass use of pirated books would likely exceed a billion dollars, with the statutory maximum stretching into the hundreds of billions.
Last week, William Alsup, a federal judge in San Francisco,
certified
a class action lawsuit against Anthropic on behalf of nearly every US book author whose works were copied to build the company’s AI models. This is the
first time
a US court has allowed a class action of this kind to proceed in the context of generative AI training, putting Anthropic on a path toward paying damages that could ruin the company.
The judge ruled last month, in essence, that Anthropic's use of pirated books had violated copyright law, leaving it to a jury to decide how much the company owes for these violations. That number increases dramatically if the case proceeds as a class action, putting Anthropic on the hook for a vast number of books beyond those produced by the plaintiffs.
Subscribe
The class action certification came just one day after Bloomberg
reported
that Anthropic is fundraising at a valuation potentially north of $100 billion — nearly double the $61.5 billion investors
pegged it
at in March.
According to
Crunchbase, the company has raised $17.2 billion in total. However, much of that funding has come in the form of Amazon and Google cloud computing credits — not real money.
Santa Clara Law professor Ed Lee
warned
in a blog post that the ruling means “Anthropic faces at least the potential for business-ending liability.” He separately
wrote
that if Anthropic ultimately loses at trial and a final judgment is entered, the company would be required to post a surety bond for the full amount of damages in order to delay payment during any appeal, unless the judge grants an exception.
In practice, this
usually
means
arranging a bond backed by 100 percent collateral — not necessarily cash, but assets like cloud credits, investments, or other holdings — plus a 1-2 percent annual premium. The impact on Anthropic’s day-to-day operations would likely be limited at first, aside from potentially higher insurance costs, since the bond requirement would only kick in after a final judgment and the start of any appeals process.
Lee
wrote
in another post that Judge Alsup “has all but ruled that Anthropic’s downloading of pirated books is [copyright] infringement,” leaving “
the real issue at trial… the jury’s calculation of statutory damages
based on the number of copyrighted books/works in the class.”
While the risk of a billion-dollar-plus jury verdict is real, it’s important to note that judges
routinely
slash
massive
statutory damages awards — sometimes by orders of magnitude. Federal judges, in particular, tend to be skeptical of letting jury awards reach levels that would bankrupt a major company. As a matter of practice (and sometimes
doctrine
), judges rarely issue rulings that would outright force a company out of business, and are generally sympathetic to arguments about practical business consequences. So while the jury’s damages calculation will be the headline risk, it probably won’t be the last word.
On Thursday, the company
filed
a motion to stay — a request to essentially pause the case — in which they acknowledged the books covered likely number “in the millions.” Anthropic’s lawyers also wrote, “the specter of unprecedented and potentially business-threatening statutory damages against the smallest one of the many companies developing [large language models] with the same books data” (though it’s worth noting they have an incentive to amplify the stakes in the case to the judge).
The company could settle, but doing so could still cost billions given the scope of potential penalties.
Anthropic, for its part, told Obsolete it “respectfully disagrees” with the decision, arguing the court “failed to properly account for the significant challenges and inefficiencies of having to establish valid ownership millions of times over in a single lawsuit,” and said it is “exploring all avenues for review.”
The plaintiffs lawyers did not reply to a request for comment.
From “fair use” win to catastrophic liability

data.title: Anker is no longer selling 3D Printers
data.author: geerlingguy
data.article_summary: Anker宣布其3D打印机业务独立为子品牌EufyMake，但目前已 indefinidamente 暂停销售其M5和M5C 3D打印机，且部分关键配件如热端也已下架，引发社区对其退出3D打印机市场的猜测。Anker发言人表示，暂停销售不排除未来推出新机型的可能性，但目前销售已停止，用户如需配件需直接联系客服。此次暂停销售可能与初期产品遇到的技术问题和市场挑战有关。其他公司如Creality也曾在3D打印机市场遇到类似困难。目前，市场上的推荐机型包括Bambu P1系列和Elegoo Centauri Carbon。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anker品牌及其3D打印机的市场表现和用户反馈

不同观点：
• [paulirwin] 对Anker的3D打印机持积极态度。他通过Kickstarter活动购买了M5打印机，并对其整体表现表示满意，尽管指出了热端设计和AI功能的不足。他认为在当时的市场中，这是一款性价比高的产品，并对Anker退出市场感到遗憾。

• [donatj] 表示惊讶，因为他之前并不知道Anker在销售3D打印机。

• [syntaxing] 认为Anker的3D打印机发布时机不佳，受到同时期Bambulab成功的冲击，否则可能会更受欢迎。

• [bsimpson] 对Anker品牌整体产生负面印象，因其Eufy robovac产品体验不佳，进而对Anker的所有产品产生怀疑。

• [Ginger-Pickles] 提供了一个存档链接，未发表具体观点。

• [voxleone] 提到一个简单的部件成为了结束产品线的战略瓶颈，但表示愿意免费提供自己的打印机以供使用。

• [nerdjon] 对Anker的3D打印机感到失望，尽管最初通过众筹平台对其抱有很高期望。他指出打印机存在许多问题，导致使用体验不佳，现在几乎不再使用。

• [OutOfHere] 认为Anker应专注于其核心业务——电池，并指出近期电池安全召回事件，质疑Anker是否能做好其他产品。

补充讨论：
• Anker的3D打印机市场表现和用户反馈存在较大分歧，有人认为其性价比高，有人则对其表现失望。
• 讨论中涉及Anker品牌的整体质量问题，特别是与其他产品的比较和品牌信任度的变化。
• 争议焦点在于Anker是否应继续在3D打印机市场竞争及其产品质量是否符合消费者期望。

Anker is no longer selling 3D printers
Sales have been paused indefinitely.
Sales have been paused indefinitely.
by
Sean Hollister
Close

Senior Editor

Sean Hollister
Jul 25, 2025, 6:34 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission.
See our ethics statement.
Image: Anker
Sean Hollister
is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget.
In March,
charging giant Anker
announced
it would spin out
its 3D printer business into an “independent sub-brand,” stating that the new EufyMake would “continue to provide comprehensive customer service and support” for its original 3D printers the AnkerMake M5 and M5C.
Now, the 3D printing community is wondering whether that was all a euphemism for
exiting
the 3D printer business. eufyMake is no longer selling any 3D printers and has stopped selling some of the parts it would need to provide anything close to “comprehensive support.”
Anker confirms to
The Verge
that it has stopped selling the M5 and M5C 3D printers indefinitely. Spokesperson Brett White could not confirm that the company will resume selling them or create any future models. He says that “sales have been paused.”
“My understanding is that eufyMake has not ruled out creating new 3D printer models in the future. But the brand has ended sales of the M5 and M5C for the time being,” White tells
The Verge
.
The 3D printing section of
EufyMake’s website
is currently empty of printers. The only gadget EufyMake now sells is a UV printer that creates a 3D texture atop flat materials.
To put it mildly, Anker had a rough start in the 3D printer business.
It set out to fix big pain points
with 3D printing with the original M5, but ran into many issues that I documented
in my original review
. The
M5C was both more affordable
and better appreciated by the community but sacrificed features like a dedicated screen. Makers ran into their share of issues with it too.
Now, Redditors are also reporting they can no longer easily obtain the most critical parts for the M5C — the hotend that melts and helps deposit 3D-printed plastic.
“Due to inventory reasons, the M5C hot end has been removed from the official website and is no longer available for purchase,”
reads an alleged email
from EufyMake support to one Redditor (hit the right arrow twice to see the screenshot):
“So my entire 3D printer is garbage because you stopped supporting it?” the Redditor replied. (Hotends are often one of the first components you replace if or typically when a 3D printer jams.)
Anker also appears to have stopped selling the full extruder assembly for the M5C. I feel for you if you bought one of these printers.
“A portion of the AnkerMake accessories for 3D printers are no longer publicly listed for sale, but customers can always reach out to the customer support team directly by emailing
support@eufymake.com
if they need any related accessories,” White tells
The Verge
. He says he’ll look into the specifics of M5C hotend and extruder availability for us.
Anker isn’t the only company that’s had difficulty moving into the next, more consumer-friendly and affordable phase of the 3D printing business. Creality also had a mess on its hands
with the K1
, a printer designed to compete with the AnkerMake M5, though it recovered from some of its issues by quickly moving to new and improved models.
Today, the friendliest 3D printers I can recommend are
the Bambu P1S
and
P1P
, and the
Elegoo Centauri Carbon
, which doesn’t offer all the same conveniences of Bambu, but meets the P1 series’ print quality, adds a touchscreen, and starts at an incredibly low price of $300. I’ve been testing my own personally owned P1P
against Bambu’s flagship H2D
and a Centauri Carbon.
While using the Bambu is faster and easier, especially with an AMS attached, I would happily buy the Elegoo if I were more concerned about
the Bambu update controversy
.

不同观点：
• **duxup** 认为，会议效率的关键在于领导层是否以身作则，设置良好的会议文化。大多数高层领导不遵循会议规则，导致整个组织的会议效率低下。
• **pjc50** 强调会议议程和会议记录的重要性，认为没有这两者的会议就像社交性质的茶话会。虽然茶话会有其社交作用，但不应占据太多工作时间。Stand-up会议常被认为是低效的茶话会。
• **keiferski** 指出，会议主要不是为了传播知识，而是为了快速沟通和决策，尤其在小团队中，实时沟通比书面沟通更高效。然而，随着团队规模扩大，书面沟通应成为主要方式。AI转录工具可以帮助将会议信息保存为书面形式。
• **pflenker** 提出两个观点：1) 会议有助于团队凝聚力，特别是在远程工作环境下；2) 会议邀请者需要明确每个参会者对会议的贡献和学习目标。
• **neogodless** 引用了Best Buy的“结果导向工作环境”（ROWE）理念，强调员工应有自主权决定是否参加对生产力无贡献的会议。
• **nickdothutton** 认为，很多会议是因为工作流程不畅而被召集的，而不是为了解决真正的问题。没有议程和明确结果的会议不应参加。
• **nxpnsv** 将会议分类为1:1会议、更新会议、决策会议和规划会议，并建议尽量将某些会议转为异步沟通或简化为单向信息流动。
• **chasd00** 强调会议需要有明确的跟进计划和决策记录，且超过10人的会议应更像网络研讨会，而非讨论决策会议。
• **FuriouslyAdrift** 将会议分为简报会议和头脑风暴会议，前者正式且不频繁，后者非正式且频繁。
• **Msurrow** 希望看到关于如何改善会议召集文化的讨论，指出很多会议是因为召集者不想自己解决问题而召集的。
• **cek** 认为大多数会议不仅是头脑风暴或决策会议，特别是在超过100-150人的大组织中，还需要有推动责任、 closure 和对齐的会议。

补充讨论：
• **javier_e06** 认为，会议让人分心，不利于创造性思维。最好的技术互动往往发生在非正式场合。
• **judge123** 指出，这些建议多针对会议召集者，而作为普通参会者很难拒绝参加没有明确目标的会议，特别是当上司在场时。

争议焦点：
• 会议的必要性及其效率问题。一些人认为会议对团队协作和凝聚力有帮助，而另一些人则认为多数会议低效且无必要，应尽量减少或替代为异步沟通。

不同观点：

补充讨论：

Home News

200,000 Flemish drivers can turn traffic lights green, but Waze and Google Maps are holding matters up
Over the past 2 years, 230 intersections in Flanders were equipped with “intelligent traffic lights”, lights that take into account how busy roads are. Today 200,000 motorists and other road users possess an app that can control such lights. But because the most popular traffic apps like Google Maps and Waze are not participating in the project, the system only reaches a small proportion of drivers and cyclists.
Colin Clapson
, opens in new tab
Published:
Thu 24 Jul. 11:03
Two years ago, the Flemish Roads Agency (AWV) announced the introduction of the new system: via an app on your smartphone, you can get a traffic light to turn green more quickly. Over the past 2 years, 250 intersections were to be equipped with so-called “intelligent traffic lights”, which would receive a signal as soon as a road user with the app approaches.
In that way, motorists - but also cyclists and motorcyclists- will not have to wait unnecessarily at red lights when less traffic is approaching from the other direction. A simple example: at night, a main road mainly displays green, the side streets only get green for a very short time. If you arrive with the app from a side street, you can get green immediately, provided there is no traffic on the main road.
The lights are waiting...
230 Flemish intersections have meanwhile been equipped with the technology, slightly less than the 250 planned, but still pretty much on schedule. "This summer we made good progress," explains Katrien Kiekens of the Roads Agency. "About 1 in 8 traffic lights along regional roads now have the technology. These are lights that are connected to the internet and communicate with road users via traffic apps, and in the future even with on-board car computers."
"We are the second country in Europe to work with this technology on traffic lights. The first country was the Netherlands. Some other European countries are trying out projects on a smaller scale. But we are among the frontrunners."
Popular traffic apps aren't following
The technology is there but needs connected users. And that is where there is an issue. Until now, only smaller players like Karta GPS, Flitsmeister and Sway are offering the ability to influence traffic lights via your phone.
"About 200,000 Flemish people currently use these apps and can communicate with traffic lights," says Ms Kiekens. "And we are already seeing the effect of that. Samples show that cars as well as bikes are crossing intersections more smoothly. But it would be better if many more people joined the system, and for that we need the big players involved."
And those big players, in Flanders, are still Waze and Google Maps. Users are not easily inclined to install an extra app, Katrien Kiekens too realises: "We want to be present on the apps that people already use. That is why we are still holding talks with the big players, to be able to make the connection with their apps."
"And not just with those traffic apps, but for example also with TomTom and with major car manufacturers to get the technology into the on-board computers of the cars themselves." But for now, those talks have not yielded any results, so you have to turn to the smaller apps.
Emergency services
The intelligent traffic light system appears already to be proving its worth especially for the emergency services. In Ghent, for example, the system is already being used in ambulances and fire trucks.
Katrien Kiekens: "These vehicles already interact with smart traffic lights, giving them a green  light.  They no longer have to cross intersections and make a dangerous manoeuvre when they are attending an emergency situation. In tests we also see that they arrive at emergencies more quickly."

data.title: Wish you could escape the planet? Too bad life in space would suck (2024)
data.author: voxleone
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了在国际空间站生活的艰辛，尽管地球上有诸多问题，但太空生活同样不易。宇航员们住在狭小空间，严格按照15分钟一段的日程生活，每天仅睡六小时，依靠湿巾清洁，饮用处理过的尿液。NASA宇航员Sunita Williams和Butch Wilmore已在空间站生活了170天，预计还将延长至八个月。尽管任务期间的死亡风险较低（1/270），长期停留会对身体造成持久影响。微重力环境导致体液重新分布，引起面部肿胀、味觉和嗅觉减退，甚至视力受损。太空生活对健康的挑战包括“太空脑”、无法正常打嗝和排尿等。文章提醒人们，太空并非理想的逃避之地。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太空探索与居住的可行性、动机以及面临的实际和心理问题

不同观点：
• [endoblast] 认为人们去太空不仅是为了逃避他人，还出于冒险、浪漫以及开辟新道路的动机。拥有正确的精神和动机能够创造心理健康，而不是依赖物质或社会条件。中世纪生活条件更差，但那时的人们可能比现代人更快乐、更有动力。

• [jameskilton] 指出人们想去太空是因为想逃避其他人，但逃离地球不可能独自完成，必须与他人一起，这意味着会带上所有试图逃避的问题。我们无法逃避彼此，只能学会共存，无论在哪里。电视剧《The Expanse》很好地探讨了这个问题。

• [libraryofbabel] 认为零重力带来的不适问题可以通过建立旋转太空站来创造人造重力解决，但这需要大量资金。辐射问题仍需解决。

• [slibhb] 将太空飞行/生活与大航海时代的帆船工作相比，指出有些人愿意忍受不适去追求名利或改变不满的现状，大多数这样的人是男性。

• [AndrewOMartin] 描述了对太空的个人感受，认为太空象征着死亡和寒冷，而地球代表着生命和温暖，离开地球是一种离开母体的体验。

• [gmuslera] 认为火星在中期内只会以不同方式致人死亡。

• [sunscream89] 提出太空生活的正确方式是重新配置人类思维，初期将非常原始和不适，需要从海洋和地下自给自足的居住开始，逐步适应任何环境。

• [taysix] 提到《A City on Mars》一书讨论了许多太空生活的糟糕方面，包括政治和法律问题，总结为“太空生活会很糟糕”。

• [natch] 讨论了Elon Musk的火星计划，认为他可能计划通过“人类继任者”即类人智能机器人来实现，而不是输送大量适应地球进化的人类，并猜测这是因为公众对机器人计划的接受度较低。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于太空探索的实际可行性和动机。一些人认为心理和精神状态是关键，而另一些人则关注实际的技术和物理问题（如人工重力、辐射）。
• 对Elon Musk火星计划的意图存在不同解读，有人认为他计划通过智能机器人实现，而不是传统人类移民。
• 对太空生活的描述普遍负面，强调了不适和风险，但也有人指出历史上人类曾有过类似的冒险和适应过程。

Wish you could escape the planet? Too bad life in space would suck
Earth can be tiresome, but you probably wouldnât enjoy living on the International Space Station either
By
Levi Stallings
Published
November 22, 2024 9:00AM (EST)
The Andromeda galaxy and an anatomy engraving (Photo illustration by Salon/Getty Images)
Facebook
X
Reddit
Email
Climate change, war and fascism got you down? Wish you could buy a ticket on the Europa Clipper spacecraft that’s on its way to
check if there’s living slime on a Jupiterian moon
? Before you decide to leave Earth behind and move to outer space, consider the life of an astronaut on the
International Space Station
.
Imagine cohabitating with eight other people in an enclosed area the size of a large airplane. You live on a strict schedule broken into 15 minute increments, using a red marker on a computer tablet to keep pace with the daily routine of experiments and maintenance all on an
average six hours of sleep
. You never shower, and instead rely on wet wipes for personal hygiene. Every human odor remains trapped around you in a cloud of stench that U.K. astronaut Tim Peake has compared to “a barbecue that’s gone wrong.” You drink processed urine. Things only get more uncomfortable from here.
Stranded NASA astronauts Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore have been
living aboard the ISS for 170 days since their departure from Earth on June 5
. Their mission, originally meant to last around a week, will have gone on for over eight months by the time the two are picked up by a SpaceX Dragon at the end of February 2025.
NASA’s accepted odds for loss of crew
during the extended stay, or the chances Wilmore and Williams won’t make it back to Earth alive, are 1 in 270. Although chances of death on their mission are relatively low, the effects of their long term stay in space will likely have an impact on their bodies for the rest of their lives.
Related
How living on Mars would warp the human body
To get a better idea of how the unexpected extra months in space may impact Williams and Wilmore, Salon interviewed NASA’s lead flight surgeon, Dr. Steven Gilmore, who supported Captain Scott Kelly during the longest planned space mission in NASA’s history: 340 days. While one mission was going on in space, another was conducted down here on Earth. NASA was monitoring changes in Captain Kelly's body while  comparing to his twin brother, Mark, now an Arizona senator, who remained on the ground during the experiment in order to determine the effects microgravity has on humans over extended periods of time.
“Essentially you can look at each of the body systems and start quantifying and characterizing the changes that the human body goes through [in space] as it's in this different environment for longer and longer periods,” Gilmore said.
"Our optometrists can estimate before they fly by what degree their prescription will change."
It’s easy to forget the joys of gravity while going to sleep or using the toilet on Earth, but the constant force that keeps us on the ground also helps us maintain bone structure and keep bodily fluids flowing where we want them. Living in microgravity causes bodily fluids to become more evenly distributed, with up to two extra liters of blood becoming unnaturally congested in the upper body, triggering constant feelings of puffiness and congestion, especially in the head and face. In Captain Kelly’s memoir, “
Endurance: A Year In Space, A Lifetime of Discovery
,” he describes the feeling of “
space brain
,” writing, “The full head sensation never completely goes away. It feels a little like standing on your head 24 hours a day, mild pressure in your ears, congestion, round face, flushed skin.”
The way fluids redistribute themselves in space is also why astronauts can’t burp without throwing up — the contents of their stomach become evenly pressed to the sides of the organ instead of settling at the bottom. This effect also causes urine to float along the sides of the bladder, which can prevent astronauts from feeling a need to pee until their bladders become completely full, leading to an unexpected, spontaneous need to urinate.

around 70 percent of astronauts who conduct long-term missions of six months or more on the ISS develop vision impairments.

44722584.article_summary: 文章探讨了在国际空间站生活的艰辛，尽管地球上有诸多问题，但太空生活同样不易。宇航员们住在狭小空间，严格按照15分钟一段的日程生活，每天仅睡六小时，依靠湿巾清洁，饮用处理过的尿液。NASA宇航员Sunita Williams和Butch Wilmore已在空间站生活了170天，预计还将延长至八个月。尽管任务期间的死亡风险较低（1/270），长期停留会对身体造成持久影响。微重力环境导致体液重新分布，引起面部肿胀、味觉和嗅觉减退，甚至视力受损。太空生活对健康的挑战包括“太空脑”、无法正常打嗝和排尿等。文章提醒人们，太空并非理想的逃避之地。

data.title: ZUSE: IRC terminal client
data.author: babycommando
data.article_summary: ZUSE是一个简洁的IRC终端客户端，使用Go语言开发，并基于Bubble Tea框架构建。它提供快速、无干扰的聊天体验，适合在终端中使用。主要功能包括简单的安装和使用步骤、基本的键绑定操作（如滚动聊天、切换窗格、退出程序等），以及跨平台支持。目前处于Beta开发阶段，可能存在bug和未完成的功能，用户可在GitHub上提交问题反馈。ZUSE还预装在Nightride synthwave radio终端客户端中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕IRC客户端及其相关话题的技术讨论与反馈

不同观点：
• **关于IRC客户端界面设计的反馈**：alberth认为当前的IRC截图对比度不够，且背景过于鲜艳分散注意力，导致难以看清内容。这表明了对用户界面设计有更高的期望，希望减少视觉干扰。
• **对IRC协议及工具的批评与反思**：dlojudice认为IRC的衰落不仅是工具问题，而是因为其协议缺乏现代团队所需的功能，如多媒体支持、文件共享、可搜索的历史记录和富文本格式。尽管IRCv3提升了扩展性，但未弥补这些功能缺陷。这反映了对IRC协议过于简陋、无法满足主流需求的批评。
• **对简约设计的赞赏**：GCUMstlyHarmls则对IRC客户端能在仅约1000行代码中实现文本用户界面（TUI）表示赞赏，认为这是对大型抽象的有效利用，显示了对简约设计和高效编码的肯定。
• **对IRC社区衰落的感慨**：boredemployee表达了对过去IRC社区中人与人之间联系的怀念，并提到最近失去了一个通过IRC结识的多年好友，反映了对IRC社群逐渐消失的感伤。
• **对IRC客户端功能性的质疑**：anonym29质疑当前Bubbletea/Lipgloss接口是否支持基本的文本操作（如点击、拖拽和高亮复制文本），指出其在这方面不如一些几十年前的CLI客户端，这提出了对现代CLI客户端易用性的疑问。

补充讨论：
• **推荐类似工具**：emersion提到了一个类似但更成熟的客户端（senpai），提供了另一个参考选项。
• **对IRC协议的怀旧与调侃**：sva_以调侃的方式称"IRC Chat"为"Internet Relay Chat Chat"，玩弄文字游戏，带有一定的幽默感。
• **对项目成就的赞赏**：haggis-alt和DigiEggz对nightrider的项目表示赞赏，表达了对开发者工作的认可。
• **对未来发展的期待**：jcastro表示希望看到类似项目应用于Matrix平台，反映了用户对IRC客户端未来发展方向的期待。
• **对技术细节的关注**：ClueslessTech99直接询问是否支持IRCv3，显示了对技术实现细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• IRC协议和客户端的简约设计既是其优点，也是其无法满足现代需求的弱点。这一观点在dlojudice的评论中尤为明显，他指出IRC因缺乏某些关键功能而被现代工具（如Slack/Teams）取代。

总结：讨论围绕IRC客户端的界面设计、功能性、社区衰落以及协议局限展开，涉及技术实现、用户体验以及对过去社区的怀旧情感。

ZUSE IRC Terminal Client
ZUSE is a sleek, minimal IRC client for your terminal. Built with Go and powered by the elegant Bubble Tea framework. Chat faster, cleaner, and without distractions right from your terminal.
Installation
go install github.com/babycommando/zuse@latest
Build from Source
Get and build:
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/zuse.git
cd zuse
go mod tidy
go build -o zuse # or zuse.exe on Windows
Add the compiled file to your system PATH
Usage
Open a fresh terminal and type:
zuse
Enter your IRC details, pick your favorite channels, and you're good to go.

data.title: How to make websites that will require lots of your time and energy
data.author: OuterVale
data.article_summary:
这篇文章以讽刺的口吻分享了几个让网站开发变得更耗时耗力的“经验教训”：

1. **随意安装npm依赖**：鼓励大量使用外部依赖，因为它们迟早会出问题，之后你需要花费大量时间替换或修复它们。
2. **在明确需求前选择框架**：使用框架会增加复杂性，每次更新都需要先理解框架的变化，从而消耗更多时间和精力。
3. **总是要求编译步骤**：在网站运行前加入复杂的编译过程，增加额外的工作量和时间投入。

文章通过反话提醒开发者避免不必要的复杂性，以更高效地开发网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的工具使用、框架选择及开发复杂性

不同观点：
• **反对过度使用ORM工具**：superasn认为，使用ORM虽然能抽象数据库操作，但往往带来N+1查询、性能问题和迁移失败等新问题，最终需要花费大量时间调试和解决。
• **工具的合理使用**：rckt认为，工具和依赖是有价值的，能够简化开发流程，比如个人网站使用Svelte等工具可以快速实现功能，而不必手写HTML。
• **开发者自律问题**：judge123指出，问题不在工具本身，而在于开发者倾向于过度工程化，缺乏保持简单的自律性。
• **新手不应过早依赖框架**：donatj认为，新手不应该一开始就依赖框架，应该先掌握基础技能，而不是急于使用高级工具。
• **多人协作中的问题**：fifticon描述了多个开发者在同一项目中使用不同工具和技术可能导致的混乱和不一致问题。
• **后端部署的复杂性**：burnt-resistor提到手动安装和配置系统可能导致的运维问题，如缺乏自动化部署、备份和应急计划。
• **框架的快速变化问题**：anonzzzies批评了像Next.js和Prisma这样快速变化的框架，认为它们会导致频繁的漏洞和破坏性变更。
• **编译步骤的价值**：card_zero和jesse__讨论了编译步骤的必要性和其带来的复杂性，jesse__认为编译语言在复杂场景中优于原生JS。
• **开发趋势的批评**：bubblyworld和sillycube认为当前的开发趋势（如使用复杂框架和工具）缺乏工程讨论和价值，并怀念像PHP那样简单的开发方式。

补充讨论：
• **幽默与讽刺**：1dom和pwdisswordfishz以幽默和讽刺的方式表达了对开发复杂性的看法，1dom甚至调侃了自我怀疑在开发过程中的存在感，而pwdisswordfishz则以加入加密货币矿工来增加开发难度。
• **简单工具的高效性**：pfoof展示了如何使用简单的Python脚本来实现编译步骤，从而减少手工工作量。

争议焦点：
• **工具与手工编码的平衡**：一部分人认为工具和框架能提高生产力，而另一部分人则认为这些工具带来了不必要的复杂性和问题，主张手工编码或简单工具。
• **新手是否应使用框架**：donatj等认为新手应先掌握基础，而另一方观点未明确表达，但暗示依赖框架可能导致基础不牢。

这些观点反映了开发者在选择工具、框架和开发方式时的多样化考虑，包括复杂性、效率和可维护性等因素。

44708270.article_content:
Some lessons I’ve learned from experience.
1. Install Stuff Indiscriminately From npm
Become totally
dependent on others
, that’s why they call them “dependencies” after all! Lean in to it.
Once your dependencies break — and they will, time breaks all things — then you can spend lots of time and energy (which was your goal from the beginning) ripping out those dependencies and replacing them with new dependencies that will break later.
Why rip them out? Because you can’t fix them. You don’t even know how they work, that’s why you introduced them in the first place!
Repeat ad nauseam (that is, until you decide you don’t want to make websites that require lots of your time and energy, but that’s not your goal if you’re reading this article).
2. Pick a Framework Before You Know You Need One
Once you hitch your wagon to a framework (a dependency, see above) then any updates to your site via the framework require that you first understand what changed in the framework.
More of your time and energy expended, mission accomplished!
3. Always, Always Require a Compilation Step
Put a critical dependency between working on your website and using it in the browser. You know, some mechanism that is required to function before you can even see your website — like a complication step or build process. The bigger and more complex, the better.
This is a great way to spend lots of time and energy working on your website.
(Well, technically it’s not really working on your website. It’s working on the thing that spits out your website. So you’ll excuse me for recommending something that requires your time and energy that isn’t your website — since that’s not the stated goal — but trust me, this apparent diversion will directly affect the overall amount of time and energy you spend making a website. So, ultimately, it will still help you reach our stated goal.)
Requiring that the code you write be transpiled, compiled, parsed, and evaluated before it can be used in your website is a great way to spend extra time and energy making a website (as opposed to, say,
writing code as it will be run
which would save you time and energy and is not our goal here).
More?
Do you have more advice on building a website that will require a lot of your time and energy? Share your recommendations with others, in case they’re looking for such advice.
