Trump's EPA argues no basis for regulating climate pollution
The Trump administration proposes eliminating a 2009 finding that greenhouse gases endanger people. That would undermine the EPA's climate change regulations for power plants and cars.
Climate
Trump's EPA wants to eliminate regulation for greenhouse gases
July 29, 2025
2:51 PM ET
Heard on
All Things Considered
Jeff Brady
Trump's EPA wants to eliminate regulation for greenhouse gases
Audio will be available later today.
The United States Environmental Protection Agency building in Washington, DC.
Tierney L. Cross/Getty Images North America
hide caption
toggle caption
Tierney L. Cross/Getty Images North America
The Trump administration announced its plan today to overturn a key
2009 Environmental Protection Agency finding
that underpins much of the federal government's actions to rein in climate change.
The EPA argues it doesn't have the legal authority to regulate greenhouse gases. The agency proposes to undo the government's "endangerment finding," a determination that pollutants from developing and burning fossil fuels, such as methane and carbon dioxide, can be regulated under the Clean Air Act.
"With this proposal, the Trump EPA is proposing to end sixteen years of uncertainty for automakers and American consumers," EPA administrator Lee Zeldin said in an
agency press release
.
Sponsor Message
Climate
Nations must act on climate change or could be held responsible, top U.N. court rules
The EPA also plans to
eliminate rules to reduce climate pollution from cars and trucks
. Transportation is the
largest source of direct greenhouse gas emissions
in the United States.
The announcement, made by Zeldin at a car dealership in Indiana, is for now only a proposal. Climate advocates vow to challenge it, first in comments during the process to finalize the proposed rule on the endangerment finding and then in court, if necessary.
"As Americans reel from deadly floods and heat waves, the Trump administration is trying to argue that the emissions turbocharging these disasters are not a threat," said Christy Goldfuss, executive director of Natural Resources Defense Council. "It boggles the mind and endangers the nation's safety and welfare."
The administration's effort comes in the wake of the
hottest year
humans have ever recorded on Earth,
dangerous flooding
in communities across the U.S.,
climate-fueled wildfires
that destroyed thousands of homes in Los Angeles and
hotter ocean temperatures
that made Hurricane Helene stronger and more likely to cause damage inland.
If the decision is upheld, it would speed President Trump's efforts to end former President Biden's ambitious climate agenda, and make it more difficult for future administrations to limit the human-caused greenhouse gas pollution that's heating the planet.
Sponsor Message
A cornerstone of U.S. climate action
In 2007 the
Supreme Court found in Massachusetts v. EPA
that the agency is required to regulate carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act. Then in 2009 the EPA, during the Obama administration,
declared that greenhouse gases in the atmosphere were a hazard to people
.
The endangerment finding is the basis for rules regulating climate pollution from
coal and gas-fired power plants
,
car and truck exhaust
, and
methane from the oil and gas industry
.
The EPA has repeatedly reaffirmed the 2009 endangerment finding. In 2022 Congress included language in the climate-focused Inflation Reduction Act that labels greenhouse gases as pollutants under the Clean Air Act. That makes abandoning the finding more difficult. Still, President Trump has made doing that a priority.
On the first day of his second term, Trump signed an executive order
asking the EPA administrator to submit recommendations
"on the legality and continuing applicability" of the endangerment finding. That echoes recommendations laid out in the
Heritage Foundation's Project 2025
, a conservative plan that aims to limit the government's ability to regulate climate pollution.
Climate
Ask your kids' camps these key questions about heat and flood safety, experts say
Zeldin first announced
the EPA's intention to eliminate the endangerment finding in March, in what
the agency called
the "most consequential day of deregulation in U.S. history."
"We are driving a dagger straight into the heart of the climate change religion to drive down cost of living for American families, unleash American energy, bring auto jobs back to the U.S. and more," Zeldin
said in a news release
at the time.
The Trump administration's position
The
Trump administration argues
the EPA, under then-President Barack Obama, established the endangerment finding in "a flawed and unorthodox way" and "did not stick to the letter of the Clean Air Act."
In seeking to reverse the endangerment finding, the Trump EPA is
making a legal argument
that previous administrators overstepped their legal authority and "imposed trillions of dollars of cost

data.title: ACM Transitions to Full Open Access
data.author: pcvarmint
data.article_summary: ACM正在向全面开放获取（Open Access, OA）模式转型，计划在2025年底实现所有研究内容的自由访问。这一转型旨在消除发现和创新的障碍，同时通过"ACM Open"框架确保出版计划的长期可持续性。该框架为机构提供无限制的OA出版，且不收取文章处理费（APCs）。定价基于机构的历史出版活动，具有公平和可预测的特点，并提供对ACM高级数字图书馆的完全访问权限，涵盖超过80万篇研究文章和多种研究工具。2026年，ACM数字图书馆将推出高级和基础访问选项，订阅ACM Open的机构将自动获得高级访问权限。高级功能包括对计算文献指南的访问、AI辅助搜索和研究影响跟踪等工具。OA文章的APC费用从700美元到1800美元不等，具体取决于作者身份和文章类型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术出版的开放获取（Open Access）模式及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **lsuresh** 认为 USENIX 会议在组织和开放获取方面表现优秀。USENIX 帮助组织整个会议，而不是依赖大量志愿者，并且所有论文都可以直接从会议网站免费访问，无需登录。
• **raphaelmo** 则更偏好 LIPIcs 系统，该系统是由德国支持的公共学术服务平台，提供了现代化的论文提交界面，且相比 USENIX 的开放获取费用更低。
• **kragen** 对 ACM 向开放获取的转变表示赞赏，但质疑其具体的许可协议。根据柏林宣言的定义，ACM 并未明确授予用户复制、分发和修改作品的权利，因此在个人网站或公共平台上分享论文仍可能面临版权诉讼风险。
• **subharmonicon** 表示因 ACM 拒绝支持开放获取，已取消其会员资格。
• **throwaway81523** 对 ACM 开放获取的具体实施细则提出疑问，尤其是关于已发表文章是否会继续被付费墙限制，以及机构和个人用户的不同访问权限。
• **bubblethink** 提到当前学术出版的价格范围（700至1800美元），认为这是不合理的“交易艺术”。

补充讨论：
• **rezmason** 以幽默的方式表达了对大量旧文档的阅读需求，并提议成立“ACM Cool Papers Club”。
• **PaulHoule** 对开放获取的进展表示欢迎，暗示这一变化是长期期待的结果。

争议焦点：
• 开放获取的具体实施和许可协议问题，特别是 ACM 的开放获取是否完全符合柏林宣言中的开放获取定义。
• 学术出版的费用问题，尤其是不同平台和会议的出版费用差异以及其对研究者的影响。

44725966.article_content:
Open Access Publication & ACM
ACM's Transition to Full Open Access: A New Era for Computing Research
For more than seven decades, ACM has played a pivotal role in advancing computing research, fostering collaboration, and disseminating knowledge through its world-class Digital Library, influential publications, and premier conferences.
In a significant step to broadening access to computing research, ACM is transitioning to a fully Open Access (OA) publishing model by the end of 2025. This bold move marks a pivotal moment in making all ACM research content freely available and removing barriers to discovery and innovation.
ACM's journey towards Open Access has been a carefully considered, phased approach, ensuring the long-term sustainability of its publications program and the various educational, diversity, public policy, and community recognition initiatives it supports.
The move to Open Access is not just a change in policy, but a reflection of ACM's commitment to its community, where the goal is to remove barriers to publishing and accessing vital research, and accelerating the pace of discovery and innovation.
ACM’s approach to Open Access is centered on 2 key elements:
1. ACM Open – A Sustainable Open Access Framework for Institutions
ACM Open is a unique and innovative take on the Read & Publish model, offering institutions a seamless way to support Open Access publishing. For academic or research institutions, pricing is based on an institution’s publishing output, averaged over the previous three years, and remains fixed for the duration of the agreement. This approach ensures predictability in budgeting while providing unlimited Open Access publishing and full read access to ACM content.
Key Benefits of ACM Open:
Unlimited Open Access Publishing
Corresponding authors from participating institutions can publish an unlimited number of Open Access articles without Article Processing Charges (APCs).
Fair and Predictable Pricing
ACM Open’s fixed term annual price, based on an academic or research institution’s historical publishing activity, ensures transparency and budget stability. This pricing model helps institutions manage costs effectively while supporting Open Access publishing. For corporate pricing,
please refer here
. For government pricing,
please refer here
.
Premium Digital Library Access
Institutions subscribing to ACM Open receive full access to the Premium version of the ACM Digital Library, providing their users with unrestricted access to over 800,000 ACM published research articles, the ACM Guide to Computing Literature (which indexes more than 6,500 3rd party publishers with direct links to the content), advanced tools, and exclusive features.
2. ACM Digital Library – A Tailored Approach to Access and Engagement
ACM is introducing
Premium and Basic
access options for the ACM Digital Library in
January 2026
, supporting a sustainable approach to Open Access. Institutions that subscribe to ACM Open will automatically receive full Premium access. A stand-alone Digital Library Premium subscription will also be available, providing continued access to critical resources and tools that support world-class computing research.
The Premium ACM Digital Library Experience
Premium
access enables institutions to fully leverage ACM content, providing deeper insights, seamless workflows, and richer collaboration opportunities for their users.
Premium
features include:
Access to the ACM Guide to Computing Literature,
expanding research beyond ACM content for a broader view of computing research.
Advanced research tools,
including AI-assisted search, bulk downloads, and citation management, to streamline discovery and workflow.
Comprehensive research insights,
including article usage metrics, citation trends, and Altmetric tracking to measure research impact.

data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 俄罗斯计划在古巴青年岛建立一个名为“数字礁”（Digital Cay）的高科技中心，目标是打造类似硅谷的技术创新枢纽，吸引超过1.5万名居民，包括专业技术人员和学生。该项目由古巴政府和亲政府媒体宣传，计划建设办公楼、实验室、住宅和娱乐设施等。然而，古巴当前基础设施薄弱，基本服务如电力、饮用水和交通匮乏，令该计划的实际可行性受到质疑。专家认为，该项目更多是俄罗斯扩大其在拉丁美洲影响力的地缘政治举措，可能涉及监控和技术控制风险。尽管古巴正经历严重的经济危机，该项目声称将为古巴数字和电信专业人士提供就业机会，但其实现前景仍不明朗。

An ambitious Russian plan promises to build a technology hub on the Isle of Youth, amid the collapse of Cuba's infrastructure.
The Cuban government announced this Friday the creation of
Digital Cay
, a Russian-backed project that aims to transform the Isle of Youth into a technological innovation center with standards similar to Silicon Valley.
READ ALSO:
Exchange rates today in Cuba: The euro continues to rise and the gap with the Cuban peso widens.
The proposal, presented by pro-government media outlets such as Cubadebate, envisions a technology cluster with more than 15.000 residents. Of these, 12.000 would be specialists and 3.000 students. The goal is to develop IT solutions tailored to Latin America and strengthen Russian industry in the region.
Dream infrastructure in a country without basic services
According to the released plans, the project includes the construction of offices, laboratories, industrial plants, residences, shops, recreational centers, schools, daycare centers, and university campuses.
However, the list contrasts with the reality in Cuba, where essential services such as electricity, drinking water, transportation, gas, and garbage collection are scarce. The project's own promoters emphasize that "high-quality communication routes" and basic services, which currently do not even operate in Havana, must be guaranteed.
More than development, a geopolitical move
Although the project is presented as an opportunity for Cuban technological development, experts warn that the Kremlin's true intention is to expand its influence in Latin America from a friendly territory.
Cuba, due to its proximity to the United States and its historical alignment with Russia, offers a strategic location for evading international sanctions and operating with greater freedom. In this context, Cayo Digital could also serve to conceal corporate identities and launch Russian products with a Latin American facade.
Surveillance and control risks
Despite the talk about “sovereign computing infrastructure,” there are preoccupied precedentscupPreviously, independent organizations have reported that similar Russian technologies have been used for espionage and political control.
READ ALSO:
Visa-free countries for Cubans in 2025: Complete list and requirements for traveling with a Cuban passport
In 2024, the Georgian government accused a Russian taxi app of transferring personal data to Moscow without authorization. And in Cuba, companies like NtechLab—specializing in facial recognition—have collaborated with surveillance systems associated with the regime's repressive apparatus.
A bet in the midst of the crisis
Cayo Digital's announcement comes as Cuba is experiencing one of its worst economic periods: daily blackouts, overwhelmed hospitals, shortages of supplies, and continued migration.
Despite everything, the project claims it will employ Cuban professionals from the digital and telecommunications sectors. Cubadebate highlighted that the José Antonio Echeverría Technological University offers training programs in Russian, which would facilitate the integration of local personnel with Russian technicians.
Stages and future promises
The project area orcupIt would cover 450 hectares. It is currently in the design phase. The first residences could be ready between 2026 and 2028, while the research centers and technology plants would be inaugurated before 2030, according to the developers.
So far, neither the Cuban government nor its media have questioned the real feasibility of this megaproject amid the national collapse.

data.title: AWS MCP Servers
data.author: belter
data.article_summary:
AWS MCP Servers 是基于 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的专用服务器套件，帮助用户充分利用 AWS 资源。MCP 是一种开放协议，用于连接大型语言模型（LLM）应用与外部数据源和工具，提供标准化方式让 LLM 获取所需上下文。AWS MCP 服务器通过该协议为 AI 应用提供访问 AWS 文档、指导和最佳实践的能力，支持云原生开发和基础设施管理。

关键更新包括：2025年5月26日，所有 MCP 服务器的主要版本中移除了对 Server Sent Events (SSE) 的支持，团队正致力于支持更优的 Streamable HTTP 传输。AWS MCP 服务器适用于各种开发环境和 AI 工具，如 Q Developer、Cline、Cursor 和 Windsurf 等。用户可通过特定配置文件（如 `mcp.json`）在不同工具中使用这些服务器。

项目遵循 Apache-2.0 许可，欢迎社区贡献。更多信息和文档可在 AWS Labs 的 MCP 项目页面找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（可能指某种API或服务）的技术实现、实用性及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [arianvanp] 认为MCP的代码看起来像是由AI生成的，给人一种不成熟的感觉。他还指出，MCP封装了许多API，但没有完全展示所有功能，这让人感到沮丧。他建议，如果亚马逊通过Smithy（亚马逊内部的协议中立API描述格式）增加JSONRpc支持，并通过Smithy生成代码，可能会得到更好的结果。

• [datadrivenangel] 关注MCP在激励机制和安全问题上的挑战，认为这些挑战可能会导致公司在初期热情消退后，因安全和商业模式问题而关闭MCP服务器。

• [blitzar] 表达了对使用MCP可能带来的高额账单的担忧，暗示了对成本控制的顾虑。

补充讨论：
• arianvanp对技术方案提出了具体建议，显示出对现有实现方式的不满，并提出了一种替代方案（Smithy + JSONRpc）。

• datadrivenangel提出了MCP在长期可持续性方面的潜在问题，特别是在安全和商业模式上的挑战。

• blitzar的评论虽然简短，但揭示了对使用成本的普遍担忧，这可能影响用户对MCP的接受度。

What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how does it work with AWS MCP Servers?
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools. Whether you're building an AI-powered IDE, enhancing a chat interface, or creating custom AI workflows, MCP provides a standardized way to connect LLMs with the context they need.
—
Model Context Protocol README
An MCP Server is a lightweight program that exposes specific capabilities through the standardized Model Context Protocol. Host applications (such as chatbots, IDEs, and other AI tools) have MCP clients that maintain 1:1 connections with MCP servers. Common MCP clients include agentic AI coding assistants (like Q Developer, Cline, Cursor, Windsurf) as well as chatbot applications like Claude Desktop, with more clients coming soon. MCP servers can access local data sources and remote services to provide additional context that improves the generated outputs from the models.
AWS MCP Servers use this protocol to provide AI applications access to AWS documentation, contextual guidance, and best practices. Through the standardized MCP client-server architecture, AWS capabilities become an intelligent extension of your development environment or AI application.
AWS MCP servers enable enhanced cloud-native development, infrastructure management, and development workflows—making AI-assisted cloud computing more accessible and efficient.
The Model Context Protocol is an open source project run by Anthropic, PBC. and open to contributions from the entire community. For more information on MCP, you can find further documentation

data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了世界上第一架商用喷气式飞机——德哈维兰DH106 1A彗星号（Comet G-ALYP）的首飞历史及其影响。1952年5月2日，这架飞机从伦敦机场起飞，飞往约翰内斯堡，标志着喷气式飞机时代的到来。相比之前的螺旋桨飞机，彗星号提供了更平稳、安静的飞行体验。然而，由于一系列事故，该机型很快停飞并被淘汰。如今，德哈维兰飞机博物馆恢复了这架飞机的内部，重现了当年的飞行体验。博物馆还保存了二战时期的蚊式战斗机原型。文章强调了彗星号在航空史上的重要性及其最终因设计缺陷而失败的命运。

De Havilland Aircraft Museum, England
—
Today, jet-powered plane travel is easy to take for granted. We’re used to that surge of speed along the runway that pins us to our seats, those moments when we burst through ominous clouds into bright blue skies, and the gentle pings warning us to fasten seatbelts. And we’re used to arriving at our destination in one piece.
But commercial jet travel is only 73 years old. Britain’s late Queen Elizabeth II was already the monarch when the de Havilland DH106 1A Comet G-ALYP took off from London Airport — as Heathrow was then known — about 3 p.m. on May 2, 1952, carrying the world’s first fare-paying jet passengers. Over the next 23 hours, with five stops along the route, it made its way 7,000 miles south to Johannesburg.
That flight marked a huge breakthrough in comfort and speed, compared to even the era’s top-of-the-range propeller aircraft like the Lockheed Constellation. Gone were the constant vibrations and the sonic assault from piston engines. The world had suddenly, irreversibly, entered the jet age.
And the first jet-plane builder to claim a place in the skies, beating out United States rivals like Boeing, was the British aviation company de Havilland. That advantage wouldn’t last: the original Comet DH106 enjoyed only a brief reign before a series of catastrophes led its entire fleet to be pulled out of service and then tested to destruction or left to rot.
The DH106 1A Comet has been restored at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum near London.
Barry Neild/CNN
Generations later, the only way to experience what it was like on board those first Comets is to look at grainy black-and-white film footage or color publicity photos of smiling families sitting on board DH106 1As.
Or at least, until recently, those images were all we had. Now a gang of enthusiasts has painstakingly pieced one of those pioneering jetliners back together — with thrilling results.
‘A beautiful sight’
Into the past:
The interior of a Comet DH106 1A — the world's first passenger jet plane — has been recreated at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum near London.
Barry Neild/CNN
Comfort in the sky:
The DH106 represented a revolution in air transport, being smoother and less noisy than the propeller planes that came before. Even in standard class, seating was roomy with plenty of leg space.
Barry Neild/CNN
Flight deck:
The controls look complicated but would've been familiar to the pilots of the day, many of whom had military aviation backgrounds, having flown during World War II.
Barry Neild/CNN
Maps and mathematics:
The cockpit also included a table for the navigator, who would manually calculate position based on speed and direction. An astrolabe was fitted in the ceiling of the plane so that the navigator could also take position readings using the stars.
Barry Neild/CNN
Jet power:
The Comet DH106 1A was powered by four de Havilland Ghost turbo jets which were embedded into the wings.
Barry Neild/CNN
Mosquito fighter:
The de Havilland Aircraft Museum is also home to the only prototype World War II plane still in existence. The Mosquito fighter, which was made on the site of the museum, was constructed from wood.
Barry Neild/CNN
Tested to destruction:
After fatal incidents involving the Comet, engineers rigorously tested the aircraft's fuselage and found that its rivet holes couldn't handle regular changes in pressure, leading to catastrophic breaches.
Barry Neild/CNN
The world's first passenger jet plane

The de Havilland Aircraft Museum is one of the world’s more obscure repositories of aviation artifacts. Located in a belt of farmland and greenery northwest of London, close to the eternally congested M25 highway that encircles the British capital, it’s easy to miss. There are signposts, but they point to a narrow lane between hedgerows that looks as if it leads to a farmyard or dead end.
Indeed, drive down it, and the first notable sight is a grand old manor house — Salisbury Hall, built in the 16th century and once home to Winston Churchill’s mother — that usually oversees some kind of agricultural outpost. But keep going, turn a corner, and the museum reveals itself: a field filled with the hulks of old airplanes and a series of hangars that hint at more treasures inside.
The site itself is a piece of aviation history. It was here, during World War II, that a local aircraft manufacturer, founded by British aviation pioneer Geoffrey De Havilland, began work to create and test the DH98 Mosquito, an unusual wood-framed combat plane renowned

data.title: YouTube rolls out age-estimation tech to identify US teens
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: YouTube宣布将在美国推出年龄估算技术，以识别青少年用户并提供更适龄的体验。该技术通过多种信号估算用户年龄，而不仅依赖用户注册时填写的生日信息。被识别为青少年的用户将受到额外保护，包括禁用个性化广告、限制某些内容的重复观看以及提供屏幕时间和就寝提醒等数字健康工具。如果系统错误地将成年用户识别为未成年人，用户可通过信用卡、政府ID或自拍验证年龄。该技术将逐步向部分美国用户推出，并根据效果进一步推广。此举是YouTube为提升青少年用户安全性的最新措施，此前已推出YouTube Kids和监督账户等功能。与此同时，美国一些州也正通过立法来规范未成年人使用社交媒体。英国本周也开始实施年龄验证检查。

YouTube on Tuesday announced it’s beginning to roll out age-estimation technology in the U.S. to identify teen users in order to provide a more age-appropriate experience. The company says it will use a variety of signals to determine the users’ possible age, regardless of what the user entered as their birthday when they signed up for an account.
When YouTube identifies a user as a teen, it
intr
oduces new protections and experiences, which include disabling personalized advertising, safeguards that
limit repetitive viewing
of certain types of content, and enabling
digital well-being tools
such as screen time and bedtime reminders, among others.
These protections already exist on YouTube, but have only been applied to those who verified themselves as teens, not those who may have withheld their real age. For instance, in 2023,
YouTube began limiting repeated viewing of videos
that could trigger body image issues or those that display social aggression. The company has also been developing
digital well-being tools since 2018
.
If the new system incorrectly identifies a user as under 18 when they are not, YouTube says the user will be given the option to verify their age with a credit card, government ID, or selfie. Only users who have been directly verified through this method or whose age has been inferred to be over 18 will be able to view the age-restricted content on the platform.
The machine learning-powered technology will begin to roll out over the next few weeks to a small set of U.S. users and will then be monitored before rolling out more widely, the company says.
The plans to introduce age inference technology were
announced in February
as part of YouTube’s 2025 roadmap. The plans are also the latest step in attempting to make YouTube safer for younger users, following the
2015 launch of the YouTube Kids app
and the
2024 rollout of supervised accounts
. The features also arrive as social media more broadly is coming under increased government scrutiny in the United States, where platform makers, including Apple and Google,
have pitted their lobbyists against those from big tech companies
like Meta over who’s responsible for age verification and children’s safety.
In the meantime, a handful of U.S. states have taken matters into their own hands, as
over a dozen
states have passed or proposed laws to regulate minors’ use of social media. Many of these require age verification or parental consent, including those in Louisiana, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Utah, Texas, Maryland, Tennessee, and Connecticut, among others. (However, some laws, like those in Utah and Arkansas, are blocked by litigation at this time and are not enforceable, while others are still pending implementation.)

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者在2024年春季启动的一个家庭项目——脱离谷歌服务。由于对谷歌依赖的反感日益增强，项目取得了一些进展，但速度不快。作者列出了一张替代服务表，涵盖办公、数据分享、照片、视频会议、地图、浏览器、搜索、聊天、照片编辑、车载界面和音乐/电视等方面，并用颜色标注了对替代服务的满意度。文章详细讨论了每个方面的替代选项和进展，例如考虑用Proton替代Google Workspace，用Dropbox替代Google Photos，以及用Jitsi或Signal替代Google Meet。作者还提到了一些选择标准，如不广告支持、非风投资金支持、非谷歌/微软/亚马逊产品，并表示开源性虽然重要但不如前三个标准关键。总体而言，项目虽然有进展，但仍面临诸多挑战。

Pink indicates a strong desire to get off the incumbent service, green means we’re happy-ish with what we’re using, and blue
means that, happy or not, it’s not near the top of the priority list.
I’ll reproduce the metrics we care about when looking to replace Google products, some combination of:
Not ad-supported
Not VC-funded
Not Google, Microsoft, or Amazon
The list used to include “Open Source” but I decided that while that’s good, it’s less important than the other three criteria.
Now let’s walk down the chart.
Office
·
This is going to be a wrenching transition; we’ve been running the family on Google stuff forever, and I anticipate
muscle-memory pain. But increasingly, using Google apps feels like being in enemy territory. And, as I said last time, I
will not be sorry to shake the dust of Google Drive and Docs from my heels, I find them clumsy and am
always having trouble finding something that I know is in there.
While I haven’t dug in seriously yet, I keep hearing reasonably-positive things about Proton, and nothing substantive to
scare me away.  Wish us luck.
Data sharing (progress!)
·
Dropbox is, eh, OK. It doesn’t seem actively evil, there’s no advertising, and the price is low.
Photos
·
We’re a four-Android family including a couple of prolific photographers, and everything just gets pumped into Google and
then it fills up and then they want more money.  If we could configure the phones to skip Google and go straight to Dropbox,
that would be a step forward.
Video meetings
·
Google meet isn’t painful but I totally suspect it of data-mining what should be private conversations. I’m getting the
feeling that the technical difficulty of videoconferencing is going steadily down, so I’m reasonably optimistic that
something a little less evil will come along with a fair price.
Maps
·
The fear and loathing that
I started feeling in 2017
grows only stronger.  But replacements
aren’t obvious.
It’s a pity, maps
and directions and reviews feel like a natural monopoly that should be a public utility or something, rather than a corporate moat.
Browser (progress!)
·
Chrome has seriously started making my flesh crawl; once again, enemy territory. Fortunately, there are lots of good options;
Even people like us who have multiple lives we need to keep separate can find enough better browsers out there.
Maybe I’ll have a look at one of the new genAI-company browsers ha ha just kidding.
Search
·
The reports on Kagi keep being positive and giving it a try is definitely on the To-Do list.
Chat
·
Signal is the only sane choice at this point in history for personal use.
Photo editing
·
Adobe’s products are good, and I’m proficient and happy with Lightroom, but they are definitely suffering from bad genAI
craziness. Also the price is becoming unreasonable.
I’ve had a few Lightroom software failures in recent months and if that
becomes a trend, looking seriously at the alternatives will move to the top of the priority list.
In-car interface
·
It’s tough, Android Auto is a truly great product. I think I’m stuck here for now, particularly given that I plan to be
driving a
2019-model-year car
for the foreseeable future. Also, it
supports my music apps.

more or less completely lost the ability to suggest good new stuff.

about having

data.title: Defending against account takeovers with passkeys and DBSC
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何通过增强身份验证和安全措施防御账户接管，重点介绍了使用密钥（passkeys）和设备绑定会话凭证（DBSC）应对当前主要安全威胁。文章指出，钓鱼攻击和凭证盗窃日益猖獗，尤其是cookie和认证令牌的盗窃增加显著。为应对这些威胁，Google Workspace推出了三项安全增强措施：

1. **密钥支持**：现已向超过1100万用户提供，具备防钓鱼和更强安全性的无密码登录方式，并允许管理员审核注册和限制使用实体安全密钥。
2. **设备绑定会话凭证（DBSC）**：目前在开放测试阶段，加强登录后的会话保护，防止其他设备使用被盗会话cookie。
3. **共享信号框架（SSF）接收器**：即将推出封闭测试，用于实时接收安全信号，帮助检测和应对风险变化。

这些措施旨在提升Google Workspace用户的安全性，有效防御账户接管风险。

44725402.article_content:
Identity and Security
Defending against account takeovers from today’s top threats with passkeys and DBSC
July 29, 2025
Andy Wen
Senior Director, Product Management, Workspace
Google Workspace Newsletter
Keep up with the evolving future of work and collaboration with insights, trends, and product news.
SIGN UP
Over the past year, defenders have been facing heightened pressure on two fronts. First, attackers are intensifying their phishing and credential theft methods, which drive
37%
of successful intrusions. Second, we’ve seen an exponential rise in cookie and authentication token theft as a preferred method for attackers, with an
84%
increase in email-delivered infostealers in 2024 compared to the previous year. That trend has only intensified in 2025.
Today, we’re sharing three enhancements in account security to help organizations mitigate these types of attack vectors.
Passkey support is now generally available to more than 11 million Google Workspace customers, with expanded admin capabilities to audit enrollment and restrict passkeys to physical security keys.
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) is now available in open beta to bolster protections after sign-in.
Later this year, we will introduce a shared signals framework (SSF) receiver in a closed beta for select customers and partners to evaluate and provide feedback.
These advancements can meaningfully enhance account security, marking a major step forward in defending against account takeovers for Google Workspace customers. Let’s take a closer look.
An easier and more secure way to sign in
Passkeys
are a passwordless sign-in method that can offer users a convenient and secure authentication experience across websites and apps. Unlike passwords, which can be guessed, stolen, or forgotten, passkeys are unique digital credentials tied to a user’s device. Here are some of the benefits of passkeys:
Phishing resistance:
Passkeys are inherently more phishing-resistant because users cannot be tricked into handing over passkeys to a malicious actor.
Ease of use:
Signing in with passkeys is as simple as unlocking your device, such as using a PIN or biometrics such as a fingerprint or facial recognition.
Strong security:
Unlike passwords that are often re-used, each passkey is unique and generated for each specific website or service.
Signing into a personal or work Google Account with a passkey on a mobile device
Signing in with passkeys is 40% faster than passwords for Workspace users.
To date, we have millions of users across enterprises, nonprofits, and educational institutions benefiting from using passkeys.
“We realized, as always in security, you have to keep moving, keep improving,” said
Odi Iancu, Executive Director of Enterprise Systems & Cloud Platforms at Wake Forest University
.
“But we have the tools available to us in Google Workspace for Education Plus to improve our security posture even further by moving to phishing-resistant second factor, leveraging security keys and passkeys.”
To learn more about Wake Forest University’s experience with Google Workspace, read their
customer story
.
Securing your account after sign-in
To further enhance account defenses after sign-in, we are adding an innovative protection to our security arsenal: Device Bound Session Credentials (
DBSC
). Available in the Chrome browser on Windows, DBSC strengthens security after you are logged in and helps bind a session cookie — small files used by websites to remember user information — to the device a user authenticated from.
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) provides:
Enhanced post-authentication protection:
Helps ensure only the originating device can access the active session.
Reduced risk of cookie theft:
Makes it meaningfully harder for stolen session cookies to be exploited on other devices by malicious actors.
Strengthened session integrity:
Helps bolster protections further with more granular account attributes when used together with
context-aware access
(CAA), even if an attacker obtains login credentials after the initial login.
Some of our customers have already begun using DBSC to protect their Workspace users, with more customers looking forward to leveraging the expanded functionality with context-aware access (CAA).
Admin console UI for the Google session control section to enable Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
Securing user accounts when a change in risk is detected
While passkeys and DBSC make it markedly more difficult for bad actors to gain unauthorized account access, being able to secure user accounts when a change in risk has been detected is essential. To that end, we are developing a receiver to consume security signals from security partners. The
Shared Signals Framework (SSF)
is an OpenID standard designed to enable platforms to exchange crucial security signals in near real-time. This framework acts as a robust system for "transmitters" to promptly inform "receivers" about significant events, facilitating a coordinate

data.title: EPA to revoke endangerment finding, the basis for regulating greenhouse gases
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 美国环境保护署（EPA）提议撤销2009年一项关键的科学结论，即六种温室气体对公共健康构成威胁，需根据《清洁空气法》进行监管。这一结论是监管汽车等排放源的科学依据。EPA局长Lee Zeldin宣布此决定，称其为“美国历史上最大的放松监管行动”，旨在恢复消费者选择权并降低生活成本。撤销该结论将取消所有相关温室气体排放法规，预计每年为美国人节省540亿美元。然而，EPA自己的报告显示，限制汽车和卡车排放预计在未来30年内产生超过2.1万亿美元的净收益。此举引发广泛批评，认为在气候变化影响日益严重之际，撤销结论是“刑事上的疏忽”。该决定的合法性受到质疑，最高法院曾裁定温室气体可作为空气污染进行监管。

EPA proposes rollback of pollution limits
Details on Trump EPA proposal to roll back Biden-era pollution limits
03:51
The
Environmental Protection Agency
has decided to revoke a key scientific finding it published 16 years ago that six greenhouse gases are a threat to public health and must be regulated under the Clean Air Act.
Known as the "
endangerment finding
," it is the 2009 scientific basis for which the EPA has regulated greenhouse gas emissions from new motor vehicles, as well as other sources of climate pollution, but Administrator Lee Zeldin announced on
a conservative podcast
Tuesday that the agency is revoking the finding, calling it, "the largest deregulatory action in the history of America."
Since it was signed by then-Administrator Lisa Jackson in 2009, the finding has been used by the EPA to regulate sources of climate change-causing pollution from cars, power plants and other sources of transportation like planes, as well as oil and gas operations.
But Tuesday, the EPA
issued a press release
saying if the draft to revoke the finding is finalized, it would "repeal all resulting greenhouse gas emissions regulations for motor vehicles and engines, thereby reinstating consumer choice and giving Americans the ability to purchase a safe and affordable car for their family while decreasing the cost of living on all products that trucks deliver."
During his appearance on the "Ruthless Podcast," Zeldin criticized the endangerment finding, saying it put too many regulatory restrictions on transportation and stationary sources of greenhouse gas pollution.
"There are people, who in the name of climate change, are willing to bankrupt the country," he said.
Zeldin also said regulating climate pollution costs Americans too much money. If the proposed finding is finalized, it "is expected to save Americans $54 billion in costs annually through the repeal of all greenhouse gas standards," according to the EPA press release.
But the EPA's own
regulatory impact report
says limiting emissions for cars and trucks is expected to generate more than $2.1 trillion in net benefits over the next 30 years, including $820 billion in fuel savings and $1.8 trillion in public health and climate benefits.
Repealing the finding comes at a time when climate change impacts appear to be reaching new heights as 2024 was the hottest year on record, and natural disasters are growing more intense,
destructive
and deadly. Since 2010, there have been 246 billion-dollar disasters striking every U.S. state, causing more than $1.7 trillion in damages, and killing more than 7,700 people,
according to archived data from NOAA
.
"For the EPA to repeal the 2009 finding borders on criminal negligence," said Robert Howarth, a professor of ecology and environmental biology at Cornell University, in a statement. "The science was clear in 2009 and has become much stronger and clearer since: climate disruption is a large and growing problem; it is caused primarily from our use of fossil fuels and the resultant emissions of carbon dioxide and methane; and it is a deadly problem."
Legality of the endangerment finding
In 2007, the Supreme Court ruled in
Massachusetts v. EPA
that greenhouse gases are a form of air pollution that can be regulated under the Clean Air Act, but it tasked the EPA with making a scientific finding about whether the gases harm public health.
Two years later, the EPA published the endangerment finding, relying on extensive scientific evidence and public input to definitively state that greenhouse gases, which cause climate change, threaten health and the welfare of current and future generations.
"I think it's the most impactful thing I worked on in my career," said a former EPA employee who was a key author on the 2009 endangerment finding and requested anonymity because of current contractual obligations with the federal government.
"This body of scientific evidence met the endangerment test of the Clean Air Act," he told CBS News. "It has stood the test of time and the science has only gotten stronger."
The EPA's new proposal aims to question the agency's ability to set standards for car emissions, according to the press release. The full draft of the rule is not yet accessible on the EPA website or federal register to review.
The release also said the EPA will "update scientific data and challenge the assumptions" of the 2009 finding with an upcoming study from the Department of Energy's 2025 Climate Work Group, which is not yet available.
Plenty of conservative groups and attorneys general have tested the legality of the finding and were pleased with Tuesday's announcement.
"Over the last four years, conservative state attorneys general were the last line of defense in fighting back against the Biden administration's federal overreach and green new scam agenda," said Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita in a statement.

44726832.article_summary: 美国环境保护署（EPA）提议撤销2009年一项关键的科学结论，即六种温室气体对公共健康构成威胁，需根据《清洁空气法》进行监管。这一结论是监管汽车等排放源的科学依据。EPA局长Lee Zeldin宣布此决定，称其为“美国历史上最大的放松监管行动”，旨在恢复消费者选择权并降低生活成本。撤销该结论将取消所有相关温室气体排放法规，预计每年为美国人节省540亿美元。然而，EPA自己的报告显示，限制汽车和卡车排放预计在未来30年内产生超过2.1万亿美元的净收益。此举引发广泛批评，认为在气候变化影响日益严重之际，撤销结论是“刑事上的疏忽”。该决定的合法性受到质疑，最高法院曾裁定温室气体可作为空气污染进行监管。

44727812.article_content:
Have you ever wanted to build your own reasoning model but thought it was too complicated or required massive resources? Think again. With NVIDIA’s powerful tools and datasets, you can train a small, effective reasoning model in
about 48 hours
, all
on a single GPU
. Even better, we’ve made all the code available to you to get started right away.
Let’s dive in.
Quick links to dataset and codes:
Hugging Face:
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
GitHub:
Data Curation Code
with NVIDIA

GitHub:
Training and Evalulation Code
with NVIDIA
NeMo Framework
Reasoning models and test-time computation
The advent of reasoning (or thinking) language models is transformative. By leveraging test-time computation scaling laws, more time is spent on generating tokens and internally reasoning about various aspects of the problem before producing the final answer. This makes them exceptionally skilled at tasks demanding deep critical thinking and reasoning, such as math and coding. This advancement signifies a paradigm shift in how language models are trained and used in various settings.
NVIDIA stands at the forefront of this advancement with its introduction of the
Llama Nemotron
family of open models, which are designed for high-performance reasoning across a broad range of tasks. To learn more about these models, check out
this blog post
. The principles discussed in this blog also apply to other leading models such as ServiceNow’s
Apriel Nemotron 15B
, highlighting the broader relevance of reasoning models in enterprise problem domains. To learn more about this model, check out
this blog post
.
From “reasoning off” to “reasoning on”: controllable reasoning modes
A key innovation of the
Llama Nemotron
models is their dynamic reasoning toggle, which allows users to switch between standard chat (“reasoning off”) and advanced reasoning (“reasoning on”) modes during inference via a simple instruction in the system prompt. This flexibility allows for optimized resource utilization: engaging deep reasoning capabilities for complex tasks like scientific analysis or coding, while reverting to a lightweight mode for simpler interactions for reduced latency and computational costs.
Our open post-training dataset for reasoning
To empower the developer community, NVIDIA has open-sourced a substantial portion of the data that was used in the post-training pipeline of the Llama Nemotron models. The
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
, containing over
32 million samples
across areas such as math, coding, chat, and sciences, provides a foundation for practitioners to train their own reasoning models. This dataset is key to teaching your model how to control its reasoning mode, mirroring Llama Nemotron capabilities.
In this blog post, we’ll explore how you can leverage the
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
,
NVIDIA NeMo Curator
, and
NVIDIA NeMo Framework
to train your own reasoning language model over a weekend.
The anatomy of the Llama Nemotron Post-Training dataset
The
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
is meticulously synthesized to enhance the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Organized into distinct subsets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL), it encompasses samples from various problem domains. The following is a breakdown of the samples across different domains at the time of this writing.
Category
Sample Count

708,920

56,339

Table 1. Sample domain and distribution of the Llama Nemotron post-training dataset
All samples in this dataset are in JSON lines (JSONL) format and contain metadata such as license type, source model, as well as the Llama Nemotron model(s) trained with that sample. Each sample consists of a prompt, along with an expected response with detailed chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces followed by responses (i.e., “reasoning on”), as well as samples with direct responses (i.e., “reasoning off”). More concretely, each sample has the following attributes:
input
: the prompt(s) to the model in the multi-turn chat completions message format. It always starts with a message with the role
user
, followed by zero or more turns, and ending with a message with the role
assistant
, such as:
[
{"role": "user", "content": "Can you help me understand the Pythagorean theorem?"},
{"role": "assistant", "content": "The Pythagorean theorem states that... Does that make sense?"},
{"role": "user", "content": "Yes, but I have a follow up question..."},
#
# ... (zero or more messages),
#
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Sure, happy to help!"},
]

: the expected response from the model (ground truth), such as:
The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².
reasoning
: whether the sample is for reasoning “on” mode or not.

on

data.title: Lovense: The Company That Lies to Security Researchers
data.author: campuscodi
data.article_summary: 本文披露了Lovense应用程序中的严重安全漏洞。主要问题包括：通过用户名轻易获取用户邮箱的漏洞，以及无需密码仅凭邮箱即可接管账户的漏洞。具体而言，攻击者可以通过API请求和XMPP服务器操作，在几秒钟内将用户名转换为邮箱。此外，攻击者还能利用硬编码的密钥生成认证令牌，接管包括管理员账户在内的任何账户。这些漏洞于2025年3月报告给Lovense，但修复过程缓慢且不彻底。尽管Lovense声称已修复，但研究人员发现问题仍未解决。最终，Lovense通过漏洞悬赏平台HackerOne支付了奖金，但修复进展令人失望。

44723773.article_content:
Lovense: The Company That Lies to Security Researchers
0
viewing
July 28, 2025 • BobDaHacker
This post has been updated with new information showing the account takeover vulnerability was previously reported and allegedly fixed in 2023. See the update at the bottom. Lovense couldn't get any scummier.
What Happened
So it all started when I was using the Lovense app and muted someone. That's it. Just muted them. But then I saw the API response and was like... wait, is that an email address? Why is that there?
Just muting someone exposed their email - wtf
After digging deeper, I figured out how to turn any username into their email address.
So we had two big problems:
Email Disclosure
- Any username could be turned into their email address
Account Takeover
- Make auth tokens with just an email, no password needed
How Bad Was It?
The Email Thing (not fixed)
The email disclosure vulnerability was surprisingly straightforward once you understood the flow. Here's exactly how it worked:
The Attack Steps:
Get a GToken with encryption parameters:
Make a POST request to
/api/wear/genGtoken
with your account credentials
This returns a gtoken and encryption keys (x and y parameters)
Look up any username:
Take any Lovense username you want to get the email for
Encrypt the username using AES-CBC with the keys from step 1
Send POST request to
/app/ajaxCheckEmailOrUserIdRegisted?email={encrypted_username}
Include your gtoken and X parameter in headers
Get the encrypted user data:
The API returns encrypted user information including a fake email
Decrypt the response using the same AES-CBC keys
Extract the real email through XMPP manipulation:
Connect to Lovense's XMPP server using your account
Take the fake email from step 3's API response and convert it to XMPP JID format (@ replaced by !!!, add _w suffix)
Example:
cfc561791785b996b989593402dc41a8!!!lovense.remote.email_w@im.lovense.com
Add this fake JID as a contact to your XMPP roster
Send a presence subscription request to that JID
Fetch your roster - this returns both the fake JID you added AND the user's actual JID with their real email
Example real JID:
xyzeva!!!riseup.net_w@im.lovense.com
(which reveals the real email:
xyzeva@riseup.net
)
The XMPP server links them by ofId, so you can match and extract the real email
Remove the contact to clean up
The whole process took maybe 30 seconds per username manually, with the script we made though to automate it, it took less than 1 second for a username to be converted to an email. We could have easily harvested emails from any public username list. This is especially bad for cam models who share their usernames publicly but obviously don't want their personal emails exposed.
Taking Over Accounts (partially fixed)
While Eva and I were checking out the Lovense Connect app later, we found something even worse (Eva did most of the work) - it was making gtokens (auth tokens) without ever asking for a password. Just an email was enough.
The Attack Steps:
Get the target's email
- Either from the email disclosure bug or if you already know it
Set up the request parameters:
userName
: The target's email
userType
: "0"
pf
: "connect-pc" (platform)
ver
: "1.7.9" (version)
Generate the signature:
Create an MD5 hash of:
{platform}-#-{version}-#-{email}##0
Append timestamp:
{md5hash}-#-{timestamp}
Encrypt the signature
using AES-CBC with:
Key: The app's hardcoded appId (
a79643e665bb9833
)
IV: The app's hardcoded appSecret (
2DF65319C4D46284
)
Send POST request
to
https://apps.lovense-api.com/api/connect/genGtoken
Get back a valid gtoken
- No password needed!
These tokens worked on:
Lovense Extension
Lovense Connect
StreamMaster
Cam101 (through the login link)
Even admin accounts
Cam models use these tools for work, so this was a huge deal. Literally anyone could take over any account just by knowing the email address.
The Timeline (Get Ready for This)
March 26, 2025
: We reported both bugs to Lovense with help from Internet of Dongs.
March 26, 2025
: They said they're looking at it.
March 27, 2025
: They confirmed the bugs exist and they're working on fixes.
March 28, 2025
: We also put both bugs on HackerOne.
April 8, 2025
: On HackerOne:
Email bug: They said it's "already known and fixed in new version" (not released yet). Paid $1,000 total.
Account takeover: They downgraded it from critical to high saying it "doesn't involve database access." Also paid $1,000.
April 9, 2025
: After we explained you can literally take over ANY account including admins, they finally made it critical and added $2,000.
May 30, 2025
: We told them nothing was fixed.
June 4, 2025
: This is where it gets insane. They said:
Account takeover was "fixed on April 7" (it wasn't)
For the email leak, here's a snippet from their email:
"Following your report, we conducted a thorough investigation and rolled out initial mitigation steps, including a temporary fix for the script path issue you identified. However, resolving the root cause involves deeper architectur

• **dizhn**：从隐私和安全的角度出发，特别指出作为一家远程操控情趣用品的公司，应该更加注重隐私和安全问题，隐含对该公司处理用户隐私能力的质疑。

• **noboostforyou**：假设chmod775的描述属实，认为这种行为极其荒谬，属于公司不负责任的表现。

• **breakingcups**：认为这种技术实践如果发生在受监管的行业，已经达到了恶意实践和失职的程度，隐含对该公司不专业行为的强烈谴责。

• **ykonstant**：进一步扩展了隐私和安全问题，指出使用该公司设备的用户可能有很高的隐私需求，尤其是公众人物，而该公司在隐私保护方面的不足可能会给用户带来严重风险，甚至超出账号接管问题本身。

• **jterrys**：通过链接提供了一个存档页面，可能指向相关事件的更多信息，但没有明确表达立场。

• **JohnMakin**：质疑公司设立漏洞奖励机制的意义，如果公司对待安全报告的态度如此糟糕，那么这种奖励机制只是形式。

• **tristor**：认为公司的行为属于故意疏忽，甚至应该让公司领导承担法律责任，公司应被政府强制解散。这是一种非常严厉的批评，认为公司不仅技术管理不当，还涉及法律和道德责任。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该公司技术架构的过度复杂性和隐私安全问题。一方面，chmod775详细描述了过度工程化带来的技术混乱；另一方面，其他评论者集中批评了公司在处理用户隐私和安全方面的不足，尤其是涉及情趣用品这种敏感行业。

• 一些评论者（如tristor和breakingcups）认为这种行为不仅仅是技术失误，而是严重的失职，甚至应该追究法律责任。

• 链接分享（jterrys）提供了进一步阅读的资料，但未深入讨论具体立场。

主要讨论点：通过微波炉加热食物的特殊效果及其合理性

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 认为微波加热食物类似于通过食物作为介电材料传递交流电，并具体描述了一种现象：面包内部会变棕色，而外部保持白色。他还提到需要精确控制时间，否则面包会冒烟。

• [reverendsteveii] 表示蒸面包已有几百年历史，认为[kazinator]描述的微波技巧是个新颖的尝试，但并不是全新的概念。

• [kelseyfrog] 提到这类似于制作日式面包屑（Panko）的方法，暗示这种微波技巧可能与某些传统食品制作方法有相似之处。

• [Detrytus] 质疑这种做法的合理性，认为面包的表皮（即外壳）是最好吃的部分，因此不理解为什么有人会选择让内部变棕色而让外壳保持白色。

补充讨论：
• [kazinator] 关注微波加热过程中食物内部和外部的不同反应，强调对加热时间的精确控制。
• [reverendsteveii] 将微波技巧与历史悠久的蒸面包技术相比较，认为这是一种新颖但非全新的技巧。
• [kelseyfrog] 通过将该技巧与Panko制作方法相联系，提供了一个实际应用的例子。
• [Detrytus] 提出了对该技巧的质疑，认为面包的外壳是其精华部分，因此不认同这种加热方式的合理性。

争议焦点：主要集中在是否有必要通过微波让面包内部变棕色而外部保持白色，以及这种做法是否影响了食物的最佳口感。

data.author: qsort
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在红队与蓝队框架下的应用及其在软件开发和安全测试中的作用。

不同观点：
• _alternator_: 认为LLM在添加测试方面有价值，因为测试便宜且易于修改，但在修复错误或添加功能时可能会作弊或写出不健壮的代码。
• recipe19: 认为仅依赖单一防御层是天真且危险的，应该有多层防御，因为不可能通过单一层次达到100%的安全。
• ants_everywhere: 认为AI在红蓝队都有用，且引用了AlphaEvolve作为红蓝队方法的例子，同时指出了安全系统的强度取决于层次和并行元素。
• ashton314: 通过RSA算法的例子说明红蓝队方法在数学中的应用。
• javier_e06: 认为在软件开发中，编码和测试不是两个对等的 forces，测试本身也是代码，也有可能存在错误。
• nostrademons: 从商业角度分析，蓝队行业比红队行业更具经济价值，因为蓝队确保基础服务运行，而红队则是附加的。
• furyofantares: 提到开放模式和封闭模式的思维方式，认为创意生成和批判应在不同阶段进行，类似于写作和游戏设计中的团队分工。
• mathattack: 认为LLM更适合用于“批判我的草稿”而不是“写第一稿”，因为LLM的建议需要手动检查。
• jacobjwebber: 认为创意的关键在于“筛选想法”而不是生成想法。
• TheGRS: 认为代理模型应参与红蓝队及管理任务，开发者更多是监督角色。
• spoaceman7777: 认为LLM更适合蓝队，因为人类更擅长红队。
• pamelafox: 分享了使用LLM进行自动化红队测试的经验，通过 adversarial LLM 和各种包来测试应用程序的响应。
• LeifCarrotson: 认为红队的重要性在于防止部署不安全的系统，但有些人为了短期利润而选择不进行测试和安全措施。
• resters: 提出LLM的上下文大小和推理能力之间的权衡，认为不同任务需要不同特性的LLM。
• zkmon: 认为红队不是单独的队伍，而是背景环境，进化通过前台和背景的互动和适应发生。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在红蓝队中的具体应用实例，如RSA算法和AlphaEvolve项目。
• 强调了多层次防御在安全系统中的重要性，以及在软件开发中测试和编码的不同角色。
• 提到了LLM的局限性，如不可靠性和不透明性，以及如何在实际应用中有效利用这些工具。
• 争议焦点在于LLM在红队和蓝队中的具体作用和有效性，以及在经济和商业背景下的价值判断。

data.title: Pay per crawl: Enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers
data.author: jaredwiener
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出"按爬取付费"（Pay Per Crawl）功能，让内容创作者可以对AI爬虫访问其内容进行收费。当前，内容创作者只能选择完全开放或完全封锁AI爬虫，而这一新功能提供了一种新选项：创作者可以对访问收费，从而实现内容变现。通过使用HTTP响应代码402（需要付款），当AI爬虫请求内容时，要么支付费用获取访问权限，要么被拒绝访问。创作者可以设置统一的收费标准，也可以选择允许某些爬虫免费访问或完全阻止。Cloudflare作为收费方，并通过技术手段确保爬虫的真实性，防止假冒。该功能赋予创作者对其内容的更多控制权和经济收益机会。

44726161.article_content:
Introducing pay per crawl: Enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers for access
2025-07-01
Will Allen
Simon Newton
5 min read
A changing landscape of consumptionÂ
Many publishers, content creators and website owners currently feel like they have a binary choice â either leave the front door wide open for AI to consume everything they create, or create their own walled garden. But what if there was another way?
At Cloudflare, we started from a simple principle: we wanted content creators to have control over who accesses their work. If a creator wants to block all AI crawlers from their content, they should be able to do so. If a creator wants to allow some or all AI crawlers full access to their content for free, they should be able to do that, too. Creators should be in the driverâs seat.
After hundreds of conversations with news organizations, publishers, and large-scale social media platforms, we heard a consistent desire for a third path: Theyâd like to allow AI crawlers to access their content, but theyâd like to get compensated. Currently, that requires knowing the right individual and striking a one-off deal, which is an insurmountable challenge if you donât have scale and leverage.Â
What if I could charge a crawler?Â
We believe your choice need not be binary â there should be a third, more nuanced option:
You can charge for access.
Instead of a blanket block or uncompensated open access, we want to empower content owners to monetize their content at Internet scale.
Weâre excited to help dust off a mostly forgotten piece of the web:
HTTP response code 402
.
Introducing pay per crawl
Pay per crawl
, in private beta, is our first experiment in this area.Â
Pay per crawl integrates with existing web infrastructure, leveraging HTTP status codes and established authentication mechanisms to create a framework for paid content access.Â
Each time an AI crawler requests content, they either present payment intent via request headers for successful access (
HTTP response code 200
), or receive a
402 Payment Required
response with pricing. Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record for pay per crawl and also provides the underlying technical infrastructure.
Publisher controls and pricing
Pay per crawl grants domain owners full control over their monetization strategy. They can define a flat, per-request price across their entire site. Publishers will then have three distinct options for a crawler:
Allow:
Grant the crawler free access to content.
Charge:
Require payment at the configured, domain-wide price.
Block:
Deny access entirely, with no option to pay.
An important mechanism here is that even if a crawler doesnât have a billing relationship with Cloudflare, and thus couldnât be charged for access, a publisher can still choose to âchargeâ them. This is the functional equivalent of a network level block (an HTTP
403 Forbidden
response where no content is returned) â but with the added benefit of telling the crawler there could be a relationship in the future.Â
While publishers currently can define a flat price across their entire site, they retain the flexibility to bypass charges for specific crawlers as needed. This is particularly helpful if you want to allow a certain crawler through for free, or if you want to negotiate and execute a content partnership outside the pay per crawl feature.Â
To ensure integration with each publisherâs existing security posture, Cloudflare enforces Allow or Charge decisions via a rules engine that operates only after existing WAF policies and bot management or bot blocking features have been applied.
Payment headers and access
As we were building the system, we knew we had to solve an incredibly important technical challenge: ensuring we could charge a specific crawler, but prevent anyone from spoofing that crawler. Thankfully, thereâs a way to do this using
Web Bot Auth
proposals.
For crawlers,
this involves:
Generating an Ed25519 key pair, and making the
JWK
-formatted public key available in a hosted directory
Registering with Cloudflare to provide the URL of your key directory and user agent information.
Configuring your crawler to use
HTTP Message Signatures
with each request.
Once registration is accepted, crawler requests should always include
signature-agent
,
signature-input
, and
signature
headers to identify your crawler and discover paid resources.
GET /example.html
Signature-Agent: "https://signature-agent.example.com"
Signature-Input: sig2=("@authority" "signature-agent")

data.title: Copyparty – Turn almost any device into a file server
data.author: saint11
data.article_summary: Copyparty 是一个便携式文件服务器，支持可恢复上传/下载，具有去重、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、媒体索引、缩略图等功能。它仅需 Python 环境，无其他依赖，可通过浏览器访问，支持多种协议如 HTTP、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、SMB/CIFS。主要功能包括文件上传/下载、文件搜索、批量重命名、媒体播放、RSS 订阅、QR码快速访问等。Copyparty 还支持自定义配置和多种服务器协议，提供灵活的文件管理和用户权限设置。项目旨在简化文件共享，并提供丰富的用户界面和操作体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Copyparty"软件的功能、技术实现、许可证争议以及用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对软件功能的赞赏**：
  ◦ [skibz] 通过视频演示中文件上传和下载的例子，强调了软件的强大和令人印象深刻的功能。
  ◦ [vorgol] 认为该工具被严重低估，称其为惊人的工具，并推荐观看演示视频。
  ◦ [akk0] 称赞Copyparty是一个了不起的软件，并提到自己拥有该软件的限量版光盘。
  ◦ [darkwater] 认为这是高级用户梦寐以求的工具，强调其多功能性和开发者的高水平，同时询问开发者是否使用了任何LLM/agent。

• **对许可证问题的讨论**：
  ◦ [eadmund] 引用了GitHub上的文档，讨论了SeaFile和Nextcloud的许可证问题，认为AGPL许可证保护了用户和开发者的权益，而不是一个问题。

• **对软件应用场景的扩展讨论**：

  ◦ [dmd] 起初认为这只是另一个文件浏览器，但在继续观看后表示惊讶。
  ◦ [visil] 认为这是一个令人惊叹的软件，并赞扬开发者对安全的重视。

• **用户实际使用体验**：

44711519.article_summary: Copyparty 是一个便携式文件服务器，支持可恢复上传/下载，具有去重、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、媒体索引、缩略图等功能。它仅需 Python 环境，无其他依赖，可通过浏览器访问，支持多种协议如 HTTP、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、SMB/CIFS。主要功能包括文件上传/下载、文件搜索、批量重命名、媒体播放、RSS 订阅、QR码快速访问等。Copyparty 还支持自定义配置和多种服务器协议，提供灵活的文件管理和用户权限设置。项目旨在简化文件共享，并提供丰富的用户界面和操作体验。

data.title: Performance and telemetry analysis of Trae IDE, ByteDance's VSCode fork
data.author: segfault22
data.article_summary:
这篇文章分析了字节跳动旗下的Trae IDE（Visual Studio Code的一个分支）在性能和隐私方面的问题。研究发现，Trae IDE存在资源消耗过高的问题，例如在相同项目下运行时，其进程数量和内存使用远超VS Code和Cursor IDE。具体来说，Trae最初有33个进程，内存占用达到约5.7 GB，经过更新后，进程数减少到约13个，内存占用降至1.9-2.5 GB。

此外，网络监控显示，即使在用户关闭遥测功能后，Trae IDE仍持续向字节跳动基础设施发送数据，且数据传输量较大。这些问题引发了对隐私和数据传输透明度的担忧。尽管开发团队在最新版本中部分解决了进程过多的问题，但遥测数据传输问题仍未得到有效解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件中的遥测技术及其数据收集实践的分析和争议

不同观点：
• kiitos认为在观察遥测选项测试时，如果用户不按提示重启编辑器，就无法得出有效结论。他对这种测试的有效性表示怀疑。
• barkingcat提到TheiaIDE作为一个VSCode的替代品，具有类似的功能，并提到其被一些大公司采用。这表明存在其他具有遥测功能的IDE选择。
• fjghajkhdfgjlk对CapCut（桌面版）的遥测数据收集感兴趣，尤其是其视频编辑器的UI体验，尽管担心可能存在间谍软件。
• spyridonas建议对Kiro（AWS分支）进行类似的分析，尤其是其数据收集实践，显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注。
• cchance认为一些系统信息和使用模式的收集并不具侵犯性，并表示不介意这些数据被收集，反映出对遥测数据接受度较高的立场。
• drewbitt质疑为什么公司不愿意让用户关闭遥测，暗示对用户选择权的关注。
• asciii对分析中的过程表示赞赏，并猜测减少进程数量可能与增加的端点活动有关，显示出对遥测实现方式的深入思考。
• hollowonepl偏好使用TUI（如helix editor）并提到ZED可能包含遥测，显示出对遥测技术的警惕。
• happycodinggg详细解释了遥测数据与间谍软件的区别，强调了透明度、匿名性和用户可选性是关键问题，反驳了一些对遥测技术的误解。
• theusus指出讨论中未明确提到是哪一个IDE，提示可能存在误解或混淆。
• efitz建议使用pi-hole来阻止遥测端点，并提到对公司忽视用户偏好的不满，表明了一种主动防御遥测的策略。
• raverbashing对使用Bytedance的VSCode分支表示不理解，暗示对某些公司的不信任。
• leetbulb担心遥测事件可能被用来泄露任意数据，如源代码，显示出对遥测技术潜在滥用的担忧。
• drewbitt提供了一个GitHub链接，指出其中没有遥测，提供了一个具体的例子来讨论遥测的存在与否。
• isatty质疑为什么人们选择使用被认为是间谍软件的软件，而不是免费软件，反映出对开源和免费软件的偏好。

补充讨论：
• 对遥测数据的具体内容、存储方式、用户可选性和透明度是讨论的核心，尤其是其是否构成隐私侵犯。
• 不同用户对遥测技术的接受程度不同，有些人认为基本系统信息不具侵犯性，而另一些人则担心潜在的数据泄露风险。
• 对具体IDE（如Trae、Kiro、TheiaIDE、CapCut）的讨论显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注，以及用户在选择软件时面临的权衡。
• 技术解决方案（如使用pi-hole）和替代软件（如TheiaIDE、TUI）在讨论中被提到，显示出用户在处理遥测问题时的实际策略。

Performance and Telemetry Analysis of Trae IDE: A Deep Dive into ByteDance's VSCode Fork
Executive Summary
This analysis examines concerning performance and privacy issues discovered in Trae IDE, ByteDance's fork of Visual Studio Code. Key findings include excessive resource consumption (33 processes vs 9 in VSCode), persistent telemetry transmission despite user settings, and concerning community management practices.
1. Background and Methodology
During evaluation of development environments for a personal project, I conducted a comparative analysis of three popular IDEs: Visual Studio Code, Cursor, and Trae (ByteDance's VSCode fork). This analysis revealed significant discrepancies in resource usage and network behavior that warranted deeper investigation.
Testing Environment:

CPU: Intel Core™ i7-14700KF
RAM: 64GB
Test Project: Identical codebase loaded in each IDE
Monitoring Tools: System Informer, Fiddler Everywhere

44703164.article_summary:
这篇文章分析了字节跳动旗下的Trae IDE（Visual Studio Code的一个分支）在性能和隐私方面的问题。研究发现，Trae IDE存在资源消耗过高的问题，例如在相同项目下运行时，其进程数量和内存使用远超VS Code和Cursor IDE。具体来说，Trae最初有33个进程，内存占用达到约5.7 GB，经过更新后，进程数减少到约13个，内存占用降至1.9-2.5 GB。

此外，网络监控显示，即使在用户关闭遥测功能后，Trae IDE仍持续向字节跳动基础设施发送数据，且数据传输量较大。这些问题引发了对隐私和数据传输透明度的担忧。尽管开发团队在最新版本中部分解决了进程过多的问题，但遥测数据传输问题仍未得到有效解决。
44703164.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件中的遥测技术及其数据收集实践的分析和争议

不同观点：
• kiitos认为在观察遥测选项测试时，如果用户不按提示重启编辑器，就无法得出有效结论。他对这种测试的有效性表示怀疑。
• barkingcat提到TheiaIDE作为一个VSCode的替代品，具有类似的功能，并提到其被一些大公司采用。这表明存在其他具有遥测功能的IDE选择。
• fjghajkhdfgjlk对CapCut（桌面版）的遥测数据收集感兴趣，尤其是其视频编辑器的UI体验，尽管担心可能存在间谍软件。
• spyridonas建议对Kiro（AWS分支）进行类似的分析，尤其是其数据收集实践，显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注。
• cchance认为一些系统信息和使用模式的收集并不具侵犯性，并表示不介意这些数据被收集，反映出对遥测数据接受度较高的立场。
• drewbitt质疑为什么公司不愿意让用户关闭遥测，暗示对用户选择权的关注。
• asciii对分析中的过程表示赞赏，并猜测减少进程数量可能与增加的端点活动有关，显示出对遥测实现方式的深入思考。
• hollowonepl偏好使用TUI（如helix editor）并提到ZED可能包含遥测，显示出对遥测技术的警惕。
• happycodinggg详细解释了遥测数据与间谍软件的区别，强调了透明度、匿名性和用户可选性是关键问题，反驳了一些对遥测技术的误解。
• theusus指出讨论中未明确提到是哪一个IDE，提示可能存在误解或混淆。
• efitz建议使用pi-hole来阻止遥测端点，并提到对公司忽视用户偏好的不满，表明了一种主动防御遥测的策略。
• raverbashing对使用Bytedance的VSCode分支表示不理解，暗示对某些公司的不信任。
• leetbulb担心遥测事件可能被用来泄露任意数据，如源代码，显示出对遥测技术潜在滥用的担忧。
• drewbitt提供了一个GitHub链接，指出其中没有遥测，提供了一个具体的例子来讨论遥测的存在与否。
• isatty质疑为什么人们选择使用被认为是间谍软件的软件，而不是免费软件，反映出对开源和免费软件的偏好。

补充讨论：
• 对遥测数据的具体内容、存储方式、用户可选性和透明度是讨论的核心，尤其是其是否构成隐私侵犯。
• 不同用户对遥测技术的接受程度不同，有些人认为基本系统信息不具侵犯性，而另一些人则担心潜在的数据泄露风险。
• 对具体IDE（如Trae、Kiro、TheiaIDE、CapCut）的讨论显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注，以及用户在选择软件时面临的权衡。
• 技术解决方案（如使用pi-hole）和替代软件（如TheiaIDE、TUI）在讨论中被提到，显示出用户在处理遥测问题时的实际策略。

data.title: M8.7 earthquake in Western Pacific, tsunami warning issued
data.author: jandrewrogers
data.article_summary: Earthquake Event Page应用支持大多数现代浏览器，用户可以查看支持的浏览器列表。此外，用户还可以选择使用实时通知、订阅消息 feeds 和 web 服务来获取地震信息。这些功能帮助用户及时获取最新的地震动态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本及周边地区海啸预警及地震影响

不同观点：
• **[decimalenough]** 提供实时信息，指出日本东部沿海面临3米高的海啸预警，并提到2011年海啸灾区此次可能再次受影响。随着时间推移，更新信息显示日本测得的最初海浪仅30厘米，且最大波浪仅40厘米，认为可能不会造成重大损害。
• **[vasusen]** 提到其妻子因一本漫画对2025年日本地震的预言而取消旅行计划，并讽刺该预言引发的恐慌。链接的维基百科页面显示，这一预言曾在2025年引发东亚地区赴日旅行的减少及航班取消。
• **[yinser]** 认为此次地震规模非常大，可能会进入历史上最大地震的前八名。
• **[andsoitis]** 提供美国西海岸的“观察”级别警告，但指出夏威夷和阿拉斯加处于警告级别，并提供相关链接。
• **[dhx]** 引用DART浮标数据，指出在某一位置观测到约1.3米的水柱高度变化，并提供具体坐标和链接。
• **[supportengineer]** 提到其在夏威夷的家人正考虑是否应返回酒店以避免海啸，并担心威基基地区可能出现洪水。
• **[mordechai9000]** 询问俄罗斯彼得罗巴甫洛夫斯克的情况，提到美国地质调查局估计该地有“严重”震感，可能有中度至严重损害及人员伤亡。
• **[bicx]** 指出俄罗斯该地区近几周有大量地震活动，并持续收到地震警报。

补充讨论：
• **[swader999]** 提供Dutchsinse覆盖的视频链接，涉及地震相关报道。
• **[watkajtys]** 提供地震的可视化链接，展示附近地震及断层运动等情况。
• **[ddtaylor]** 询问美国西海岸可能受到的影响。
• **[discordance]** 提供美国地质调查局的互动地图链接，展示地震事件详情。
• **[lordswork]** 提供加州海啸地图链接，但指出该链接因访问量过大而无法打开，请求截图。
• **[barlog]** 提供日本新闻的实时摄像头链接，便于查看实时情况。

争议焦点：
• 对此次海啸是否会造成重大损害存在不同看法。**[decimalenough]** 认为 unlikely（不太可能）造成重大损害，而 **[yinser]** 则强调地震规模巨大，可能进入历史最大地震的前八名，暗示潜在的严重性。
• **[vasusen]** 提到的因漫画预言引发的恐慌和实际地震预警之间的对比，也显示出对地震预言的质疑和现实预警的不同态度。

总的来说，讨论围绕地震和海啸的实时动态、潜在影响及历史对比展开，同时涉及对不同地区预警级别的关注和具体应对措施的讨论。

data.title: RIP Shunsaku Tamiya, the man who made plastic model kits a global obsession
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 日本知名模型制造公司田宫（Tamiya）的前社长及董事长田宫俊作于7月18日去世，享年90岁。他带领田宫从运输和木材业务转型为高精度塑料模型和遥控车制造商，尤其以迷你四驱车闻名。田宫俊作推动公司从木质模型转向塑料模型，并创造了田宫的标志性品牌形象和高质量声誉，包括著名的“双星”logo和“白盒”包装设计。他为确保模型精度，曾购买保时捷911并拆解以完善模型细节。2018年，他获得日本媒体艺术节的终身成就奖。他的贡献对模型爱好者和汽车 enthusiasts 产生了深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模型制作爱好及其变迁

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为，模型组装本身虽然有趣，但更重要的是后期 painting 和 lighting，这与现代 YouTuber 们的观点一致。他还提到模型制作培养了他的空间思维和设计心态，但遗憾这个爱好逐渐失去流行，类似于 R/C 飞机和火箭模型。
• louthy分享了自己在80年代玩Tamiya遥控车的经历，强调了那种动手改造（如增加电池包）带来的短暂刺激和乐趣，即使结果是破坏性的。
• firefax指出，模型制作是一项需要技能的艺术形式，但对某些人（如自闭症谱系的人）来说可能存在障碍。他还表达了对模型套件简化和品牌化趋势的担忧，认为这可能反映了社会过度依赖网络的现象。
• spankibalt提到在东德时期对模型制作不感兴趣，但通过铁路模型店培养了对设计和插图的热爱，强调了模型盒艺术的吸引力。
• kkylin对RC汽车技术发展缓慢表示惊讶，质疑是否因为新一代孩子对这种动手体验不感兴趣，导致技术停滞。

补充讨论：
• radpanda通过Tamiya-san的故事，幽默地质疑其购买保时捷以确保模型准确性的动机，可能与税务问题有关。
• toomuchtodo简单提到了Tamiya主席逝世的新闻链接，未深入讨论。
• mirkodrummer和esafak分享了与家人一起组装模型和玩具的怀旧记忆，强调了这种活动对动手能力和专注力的培养。
• kawsper指出Tamiya的影响已延伸至其他爱好，如airsoft和无人机领域。
• billforsternz对模型制造行业的长寿和多样性表示赞赏，并好奇是否存在如“明星工匠”这样的角色。
• burnt-resistor怀念Tamiya模型出色的图示说明书，认为其优于IKEA说明书。
• Aeolun提到在Tamiya店铺中提供的工具、空间和赛道体验，认为这是吸引人的部分，且价格合理。

争议焦点：
• 模型制作的现代趋势，尤其是简化和品牌化套件是否削弱了传统模型的魅力和挑战性。

44728188.article_content:
Shunsaku Tamiya, former president and chairman of Tamiya, Inc., passed away on July 18. His death was announced on July 21, with funeral services attended by close family and friends. Mr Tamiya led the transformation of Tamiya into a world-renowned manufacturer of high-precision plastic model kits, radio control vehicles, and motorized Mini 4WD racers.
He joined the company founded by his father originally as a transport firm, and switched to supplying lumber after the war. That brought about an expansion into wooden models, primarily of ships and planes. After a fire destroyed the company’s lumber supply, it focused primarily on the models.
Not long after, plastic technology improved and began taking over the model kit market. Shunsuke Tamiya spearheaded the shift to
puramo
(a portmanteau of “plastic” and “model”) and in the process changed the industry. He helped fuel enthusiasm for cars, as well as other types of transportation, for generations of children and adults alike.
Shunsaku Tamiya was responsible for creating Tamiya’s signature branding and reputation for quality. He invited his brother Masao to create the “twin stars” logo and hired illustrators to create the “white box” look that made Tamiya stand out in sharp contrast to the box art of other model makers.
Most of all, he was the driving force in the unmatched precision Tamiya kits have come to be celebrated for. Famously, while creating the model kit for the 1976 Porsche 934 Turbo RSR, Tamiya-san sent his designers to Porsche’s Zuffenhausen factory several times to get the measurements and details just right. However, despite repeated trips there were still doubts about the kit’s accuracy. So Tamiya bought a Porsche 911 and completely disassembled it to get every detail correct. Eventually, the car was put back together, and Shunsaku Tamiya personally ferried Jody Scheckter and his wife to the 1976 Japan Grand Prix in it.
In 2018 Shunsaku Tamiya was given a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Japan Media Arts Festival for his contributions to the hobby industry. His contributions to the imaginations of petrolheads, however, will live on for many more years to come. Shunsaku Tamiya was 90 years old.

data.title: URL-Driven State in HTMX
data.author: lorenstewart
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了如何在HTMX中通过URL管理应用状态，避免复杂的客户端状态处理。核心思想是将状态存储在URL参数中，使页面状态可书签化和共享。文章通过一个示例演示了这一模式的实现步骤：

1. **服务器读取URL状态**：服务器端点读取URL参数并渲染初始视图。
2. **使用表单和隐藏字段保持状态**：通过HTML表单和隐藏字段在不同交互中保持状态一致。
3. **自动更新浏览器URL**：利用`hx-push-url`自动更新URL，确保状态同步。

这种方法依赖于URL作为单一状态来源，通过服务器端渲染和简单的HTML机制实现状态管理，避免了复杂的JavaScript操作。CSS类和隐藏字段帮助保持和反映当前状态。

Bookmarkable by Design: URL-Driven State in HTMX
When you move from React to HTMX, you trade complex state management for server-side simplicity. But you still need to handle filters, sorting, pagination, and search. Where does that state live now?
The answer is surprisingly elegant: in the URL itself. By treating URL parameters as your single source of truth, you get bookmarkable, shareable application state without needing to install another dependency.
The Pattern in Action
A URL like
/?status=active&sortField=price&sortDir=desc&page=2
tells you everything about the current view. It’s not just an address: it’s a complete state representation that users can bookmark, share, or refresh without losing context.
Quick Start: Three Essential Steps
The entire pattern revolves around three synchronized steps:
Server reads URL parameters
and renders the appropriate view
Forms and hx-include preserve all state
when making HTMX requests
Browser URL updates automatically
with hx-push-url

data.title: iPhone cameras are good
data.author: sergiotapia
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了为什么iPhone拍摄的照片很少被印刷和展示。尽管iPhone相机表现出色，但在细节上仍与专业相机有明显差距。文章指出了几个关键问题：iPhone的鱼眼镜头会导致扭曲，尤其是在照片边缘的人物显得向中心倾斜；iPhone在处理阴影和光线时过度计算，导致面部特征失真，不如专业相机捕捉的自然和立体；iPhone的照片缺乏背景虚化（bokeh）效果，使得主体不够突出；肤色和光影处理也不如老款专业相机真实。这些细微差别对人类视觉感知影响显著，因此iPhone照片通常不适合用于大幅打印或展示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手机摄像头与专业相机的拍摄效果对比

不同观点：
• FredPret：认为专用相机（如无反相机）在搭配优质镜头时，拍摄效果远胜于iPhone，尤其是在旅行和家庭照片中。但iPhone的优势在于便携性和易用性，适合随手拍摄。
• hatthew：指出手机摄像头存在过度锐化的问题，导致细节处的色彩失真。同时澄清iPhone并没有鱼眼镜头，而是广角镜头，这种镜头只是放大了现实中的畸变。
• can16358p：认为iPhone摄像头在获取即时、算法处理过的HDR照片方面表现出色，尤其适合微距拍摄，但整体效果仍不及专用相机。
• dagmx：认为文章对焦距和色彩处理的比较不清晰，强调手机与相机在传感器大小、噪点控制和景深等方面的实质差异，而非表面上的比较。
• aosaigh：认为手机摄影在社交媒体上看起来不错，但在打印和仔细观察时，质量和编辑问题显现。同时，使用取景器拍摄有一种独特的体验。
• StrLght：认为iPhone照片在手机屏幕上看起来不错，但在放大、打印或在大屏幕上观看时，效果不佳。
• atonse：注意到iPhone视频在Apple TV上播放时出现奇怪波动，怀疑是iCloud压缩问题，并认为真实相机提供的控制和效果更好。
• tverbeure：不满iPhone对小细节的处理，认为其效果像被过度处理过。
• nixass：对Pixel手机照片在显示器上的表现失望，计划重新使用尼康D3200拍摄。
• sturza：认为手机摄影经过优化，适合手机显示，但不适合桌面观看或打印。
• bdamm：强调iPhone照片在实际应用中，因被拍摄者的舒适度和心态而显得更好，而非纯粹的技术效果。
• cunidev：认为大尺寸传感器在手机中能显著提升拍摄质量，但需避免过度AI处理。

补充讨论：
• epicureanideal：提出是否可以通过软件去除鱼眼畸变的问题，引发对镜头畸变及其修正的进一步讨论。
• aosaigh：对使用取景器拍摄的独特体验表示欣赏，认为这种体验在手机上无法获得。

争议焦点：
• 手机摄像头是否能在所有场景下替代专用相机，特别是在细节处理、色彩准确性和拍摄体验方面。
• 文章中对焦距和色彩处理的比较是否准确、合理。

总结：讨论主要围绕手机摄像头与专用相机在便携性、拍摄效果、用户体验和适用场景等方面的对比，各有优劣，取决于用户需求和使用场景。

"iPhone Cameras are Actually Really Good"
Ever wonder why you never see a smartphone photo printed and
framed on the wall? I'll explain exactly why.
The photos above look similar at a glance, but there are some key
differences that seem small but are actually very sensitive to our
perception of humans:
The fish eye iPhone lens creates distortion, look at the
feet of the pink player. There's also distortion of the
players on the edges who appear to be leaning toward the
center in the iPhone photo.
Compare the jawlines (important!) of the players. The
iPhone photo is much less flattering. Real cameras
capture shadow more accurately. An iPhone does lots of
computation to try to make everything well-lit, but it
ruins important facial features in the process.
The blurred background of the right photo makes the
players "pop". This is called bokeh. The landscape is
also much more accurate to human perception, again due
to fish-eye distortion of the iPhone camera.
Let's take a look at an individual player:
More things to notice:
in the iPhone photo, the player is "leaning". His (long)
feet are on the left and his head is on the right of the
image. In the right image, the image accurately portays
his balanced and confident stance.
The players body is much more flattering in the right
image. His chest and shoulders look larger compared to
the "stumpy" appearance on the left.
The jawline is much more flattering in the right image.
The iPhone image almost entirely deletes the jawline on
the shaded side of his face.
The iPhone has a "hotdog" skin complexion.
Off with their heads!
Looking into their headshots in particular here, notice the
following:
The player in pink has natural color in his cheeks in the
bottom photo, but the iPhone photo puts it through the
computational mixer and loses this entirely.
The iPhone fails to accurately capture the golden hour sun
in the hair of the players.
The leftmost player's head is substantially distorted by
iPhone.
The above photo is from a professional camera. Let's compare iPhone
with its mighty 48 MP to a 2004 Sony Digicam with a paltry 5.1 MP on
auto mode:
Some notes comparing the above photos:
The iPhone photo again has the "hotdog" skin complexion. The
digicam photo is more realistic and aesthetic.
The iPhone photo has worse subject-background separation.
The water in the background is actually more detailed than
reality, which is captured in the digicam photo. The iPhone
foreground is also artificially well-lit. This detail
distracts from the subject.
The digicam photo has more dramatic highlights and shadows,
and more accurately captures the lighting on the child. If
you look at the right knee on the iPhone photo, there is a
clear lighting defect computed by the millions of lines of
code in Apple's image processing software.

sensitive when perceiving other humans.

why top brands like The Masters never post iPhone photos.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件工程中的任务变异性、度量问题、架构责任以及开发者角色

不同观点：
• **thisoneisreal**：认为软件工程中的任务具有高度变异性，不能像流水线或销售工作那样简单量化。强行的量化反而会增加摩擦，使问题更严重。引用了《The Principles of Product Development Flow》来支持这一观点。

• **foxbarrington**：强调计划本身可能没有太大价值，但规划的过程非常重要。估计的价值不在于结果，而在于通过观察估计如何随时间变化，理解背后的原因，从而获得洞见。

• **bee_rider**：指出讨论应明确针对软件工程，而非一般工程。认为博客标题应更清楚地说明讨论对象，以免引起误解。

• **jongjong**：认为软件工程师实际上同时扮演架构师、工程师和建造者的角色，且工作基于他人成果，具有动态变化的特点。批评许多公司试图将软件工程师变为可替换的齿轮，而不是赋予他们管理和所有权责任，导致开发者流失和项目复杂性增加。强调软件架构的重要性，认为10x开发者的核心能力在于优秀的架构技能。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：软件工程师是否应被视为可替换的齿轮。jongjong认为这种做法导致了不负责任的开发文化和高复杂性的项目，而其他观点未直接回应此争议，但thisoneisreal和foxbarrington的观点可以间接支持这一批评，即简单的量化管理和忽视规划过程可能加剧问题。

• **readthenotes1**：质疑对土木工程师的泛化评论，暗示不同工程学科之间可能存在误解或不恰当比较，但未展开具体讨论。

• **例子**：jongjong提供了个人经历，描述了一个复杂且 poorly architected 的10年老项目，展示了复杂性和架构问题对开发工作的影响。这一例子支持了其关于架构和开发者角色的论点。

整体来看，讨论围绕软件工程的特殊性、度量与估计的价值、开发者角色和架构责任等主题展开，其中jongjong的观点较为全面，提供了具体案例和批评。

主要讨论点：睡眠障碍与肝脏纤维化、肝硬化的相关性及其潜在原因

不同观点：
• [Aurornis的观点] 睡眠障碍与肝脏疾病（如纤维化和肝硬化）有较高的相关性，这可能是因为睡眠中断会影响肝脏功能。然而，Aurornis质疑这种相关性在多大程度上是经常饮酒的间接结果，因为饮酒既会影响睡眠也会损害肝脏。
• [searine的观点] 没有直接表达观点，但指出了相关研究得到了中国多个国家级和北京市基金的支持，暗示研究的权威性和可信度。

补充讨论：
• Aurornis提出了一种潜在的混杂因素，即酒精消费可能同时影响睡眠和肝脏健康，进而质疑睡眠障碍与肝脏疾病之间的直接因果关系。
• searine强调了研究项目的国家级支持，可能意在表明该研究经过了严格的科学评审和资助批准，增加了其科学性和可信度。
